records.s: Major Sholto hears Small’s account of the hidden treasure and agrees, with Captain Morstan, to investigate it in exchange for a share and assistance in freeing the conspirators. He goes to India, finds the treasure, and according to Small steals it without fulfilling the agreement.

records.l: Captain Morstan, The Sign of the Four, He stopped, and held out his manacled hands for the whiskey-and-water
records.s: Captain Morstan is Major Sholto’s close friend and hears Small’s account before agreeing to the proposed treasure bargain. He later goes to Agra and discovers that the treasure has been taken; Small says that Morstan and Sholto betrayed the conspirators, while Morstan subsequently leaves the army after receiving an inheritance.

records.s: Tonga is an Andaman Islander whom Small nurses back to health and befriends. He owns a large canoe, helps Small escape the island with supplies, and sails with him for ten days before they are rescued by a trader.

records.s: The four treasure conspirators are Small, Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, and Dost Akbar. They murder and bury Achmet, hide his jewels in the Agra fort, swear to act together, are arrested and sentenced for the murder, and later attempt to bargain away the treasure’s location in exchange for freedom.

records.s: The murder of Achmet is committed by the four treasure conspirators after Achmet enters the fort with the rajah’s jewels. His body is hidden in a crumbling hall, but a spy’s report leads to its discovery and the arrest and trial of the conspirators.

records.s: Small escapes the Andamans with Tonga in Tonga’s canoe after arranging for supplies and a nighttime departure. Before leaving, Small kills a convict-guard who had repeatedly mistreated him, and the pair eventually reach a trader bound from Singapore to Jiddah.

records.s: The Agra treasure consists of a large collection of diamonds, emeralds, rubies, carbuncles, sapphires, agates, beryls, onyxes, cats’-eyes, turquoises, and pearls, including the Great Mogul diamond and a gold coronet with twelve pearls. The four conspirators hide it in the Agra fort, but Major Sholto later finds and takes it after betraying their agreement.

records.s: The treasure is kept in a chest that the conspirators open with a key hanging from a carved handle. They remove the jewels to inventory them, return them to the chest, and conceal it beneath bricks in a well-preserved wall of the Agra fort.

records.s: Small draws four plans marking the treasure’s hiding place, one for each conspirator, and marks them with the sign of the four. He later prepares two additional charts for Major Sholto and Captain Morstan, identifying the relevant part of the Agra fort and signing them with the same sign.

records.s: Agra is the place where Achmet is murdered, where the conspirators hide the treasure, and where they are later tried for the crime. Major Sholto travels to Agra, finds the treasure, and removes it without honoring the bargain.

records.s: The Agra fort is where the conspirators carry Achmet’s body and hide it in a crumbling hall. They also conceal the treasure chest beneath bricks in the best-preserved wall, using plans to record its location.

records.s: Blair Island in the Andamans is the settlement to which Small is transferred after serving time at Agra and Madras. Small lives at Hope Town on Mount Harriet, performs labor, learns to dispense drugs, and looks for a way to escape.

records.l: the Andamans, The Sign of the Four, He stopped, and held out his manacled hands for the whiskey-and-water
records.s: The Andamans are a remote, fever-stricken penal settlement hundreds of miles from other land, making escape difficult. Small eventually escapes from there with Tonga by canoe.

records.l: India, The Sign of the Four, He stopped, and held out his manacled hands for the whiskey-and-water
records.s: India is the setting for the Indian mutiny, the murder and concealment of Achmet’s treasure, and the conspirators’ imprisonment and trials. Major Sholto travels to India to verify Small’s account and takes the treasure from Agra.

records.l: the conspiracy's oath, The Sign of the Four, He stopped, and held out his manacled hands for the whiskey-and-water
records.s: The conspirators’ oath binds them to stand by one another, keep the treasure secret, and act together so that none can take advantage. Small insists that any escape bargain must include all four conspirators because of this oath.

records.s: Small offers Major Sholto and Captain Morstan a share of the treasure in exchange for freeing all four conspirators and providing a yacht, provisions, and passage to the Indian coast. The officers agree to investigate, but Sholto takes the treasure and fails to carry out the agreed conditions.

records.s: The narrator recounts how he and Tonga spent years trying to recover the jewels from Major Sholto and eventually learned that the treasure had been found at Pondicherry Lodge. After Major Sholto died and left no record of the treasure's location, the narrator marked his body with the sign of the four. Tonga later entered the chemical laboratory through the roof, killed Bartholomew Sholto, and helped the narrator steal the treasure-box. They escaped toward their ship in the launch Aurora, while the narrator insists that he is innocent of Bartholomew Sholto's death.

records.s: Tonga traveled with the narrator and was exhibited at fairs as a black cannibal, where he ate raw meat and performed a war-dance. He climbed through the roof of the chemical laboratory, killed Bartholomew Sholto, helped move the treasure-box, and escaped by pulling up the rope and closing the window.

records.s: The narrator spent years trying to find Major Sholto and determine whether he still possessed the jewels. Major Sholto guarded himself with two prize-fighters, his sons, and his khitmutgar, but died before the narrator could confront him; the narrator searched his papers and found no record of the treasure.

records.s: The narrator and his Sikh friends had a sign representing the four conspirators. The narrator left this sign on Major Sholto's bosom and later on the table in the chemical laboratory to show that the jewels had returned to those who claimed the most right to them.

records.s: The narrator continued to receive news from Pondicherry Lodge while he and Tonga made a living exhibiting Tonga. For some years the news concerned the search for the treasure, and later revealed that it had been found.

records.s: The narrator claims that he is innocent of Bartholomew Sholto's death because Tonga killed him. He presents his account as the truth and says he is revealing everything because he believes this is his best defense.

records.s: Sherlock Holmes concludes that Jonathan Small’s account provides a fitting end to the case, while Athelney Jones prepares to take Small into custody for trial. The narrator reveals that Miss Morstan has accepted him as a prospective husband, causing Holmes to lament that the narrator may leave their investigative work. Holmes identifies Lal Rao, the butler, as the confederate in the Norwood affair and credits Jones with catching one person. After the others receive their respective outcomes, Holmes turns to his cocaine-bottle.

records.s: Sherlock Holmes questions Jonathan Small about his account and learns that Small brought his own rope and that Tonga had retained one dart in his blow-pipe. He says that emotional attachments oppose the cold reason he values and that he would never marry for fear of biasing his judgment. Holmes identifies Lal Rao as the confederate in the Norwood affair and ends the episode by reaching for his cocaine-bottle.

records.s: The narrator says that the conclusion may be his last investigation with Holmes because Miss Morstan has accepted him as a prospective husband. He defends his choice when Holmes expresses dissatisfaction and observes Holmes’s alternating laziness and energetic activity.

records.s: Jonathan Small confirms that he brought his own rope and explains that Tonga had lost all his darts except the one in his blow-pipe. Athelney Jones takes Small away under guard, warning him not to strike with his wooden leg.

records.s: Athelney Jones insists that duty requires him to place Jonathan Small safely under lock and key, despite having assisted Holmes and the narrator. He says that Holmes and the narrator will be wanted at the trial and claims the credit for catching one person in the Norwood affair.

records.s: Miss Morstan has accepted the narrator as a husband in prospective. Holmes considers her charming and says she might have been useful in investigative work because she preserved her father's Agra plan from his other papers.

records.s: The case is described as extremely interesting, and Jonathan Small’s account is treated as its fitting wind-up. Holmes concludes that Lal Rao, the butler, was the confederate in the Norwood affair.

records.s: Jonathan Small is to be taken into custody, and Holmes and the narrator are expected to appear at the trial.

records.s: Miss Morstan has accepted the narrator as a husband in prospective. The narrator expects the marriage to affect his future participation in investigations with Holmes, while Holmes says that emotional attachments conflict with the cold reason he values.

records.s: After the case, the narrator says that he receives a wife and Jones receives the credit, and asks what remains for Holmes. Holmes answers that the cocaine-bottle remains for him and reaches for it.

records.l: The Sign of the Four
records.s: The records recount Sherlock Holmes and Dr. John Watson’s investigation of Captain Morstan’s disappearance, the Agra treasure, and the murder at Pondicherry Lodge. Holmes begins in Baker Street, defending mental work and demonstrating deduction from Watson’s brother’s watch. Miss Mary Morstan then seeks help: her father vanished in 1878, anonymous pearls have arrived yearly since 1882, and a letter promises justice. Watson is immediately drawn to her, while Holmes warns against emotion in reasoning. A paper bearing a plan, a red cross, and “The sign of the four” leads Holmes, Watson, and Mary to Thaddeus Sholto. Thaddeus explains that Major John Sholto concealed Captain Morstan’s death and retained Morstan’s share of the Agra treasure. At Pondicherry Lodge they find Thaddeus’s brother, Bartholomew Sholto, murdered in a locked laboratory; the treasure is gone and another “sign of the four” is left behind. Holmes rejects Athelney Jones’s suspicion of Thaddeus. From a poisoned thorn, small bare footprints, creosote, and access through the roof and window, he identifies Jonathan Small and a small islander later named Tonga. With Toby the dog, Holmes and Watson trace the fugitives to the Thames. After delays, Holmes disguises himself, locates the Aurora, and joins Watson and Jones in a launch pursuit. Small is captured when the Aurora grounds; Tonga is shot into the river, and the treasure-chest is recovered. The chest proves empty. Small says he threw the treasure away rather than surrender it, and tells its history: he and Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, and Dost Akbar killed Achmet during the Indian mutiny and hid his jewels. Imprisoned, they offered Major Sholto and Captain Morstan the treasure in return for help escaping, but Sholto took it and betrayed them. Small later escaped with Tonga, pursued the Sholtos, marked Major Sholto’s body, and stole the box after Tonga killed Bartholomew. Holmes identifies Lal Rao as the Norwood confederate. As Small is taken for trial and Jones receives credit for a capture, Watson declares his love to Mary; she accepts him, while Holmes returns to cocaine.

records.l: Sherlock Holmes, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Sherlock Holmes is an unofficial consulting detective and analytical investigator who has made detection his particular profession. He regards himself as the last and highest appeal when official detectives cannot solve a case, relying on observation, deduction, chemical analysis, specialized knowledge such as tobacco ashes, disguises, and irregular methods. He works closely with Dr. John Watson, employs Wiggins and the Baker Street Irregulars, and values cold reason above emotional attachment. When deprived of intellectual work, he abhors stagnation, craves mental exaltation, and uses cocaine as a stimulant. In the Mary Morstan case, Holmes begins by meeting and questioning Miss Morstan about her missing father, pearls, anonymous letters, and a mysterious paper. He connects the handwriting, investigates Major Sholto’s death, recognizes the paper’s significance, and accompanies Morstan and Watson to meet Thaddeus Sholto. At Pondicherry Lodge, he gains entry through his past boxing connection with McMurdo, examines a locked-room murder, identifies poison and the route of escape, and clears Thaddeus Sholto of the killing. Holmes reconstructs the fugitives’ movements from footprints, a rope, a poisoned thorn, and a creosote trail. With Toby’s help, he traces Jonathan Small and an unnamed associate through London, then learns that they escaped in the Aurora. When the search stalls, Holmes advertises, investigates in disguise, recruits the Irregulars, directs Athelney Jones, and locates the launch at Jacobson's Yard. He leads the Thames pursuit, stops the fugitives, recovers the iron chest formerly containing the treasure, and finds evidence of the Islander’s weapon. Afterward, Holmes questions Jonathan Small, offers help if Small tells the truth, and listens to his account with interest but also disgust. He concludes that the full justice of the earlier events cannot be judged without hearing Small’s story. The episode ends with Holmes rejecting marriage as a threat to impartial judgment and reaching again for his cocaine-bottle.

records.l: Dr. Watson, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Dr. John Watson is a medical doctor, army surgeon, half-pay surgeon, and Sherlock Holmes’s fellow lodger and investigative companion in Baker Street. Before these events, he served in the Afghan campaign, was wounded by a Jezail bullet, and suffered damage to his tendo Achillis, leaving him with a weak leg and limited finances. He is the author of A Study in Scarlet and, in this account, objects to Holmes’s cocaine use while admiring Holmes’s ability to infer a watch’s history. The record follows Watson through the investigation involving Miss Mary Morstan, the Sholtos, Jonathan Small, and the missing treasure. At Mary’s request, he joins her and Holmes, becomes strongly attracted to her, and accompanies them through a threatening expedition. He uses his medical skills to examine Thaddeus Sholto and later Bartholomew Sholto’s body, concluding that a powerful vegetable alkaloid caused Bartholomew’s death. He comforts Mary, escorts her home, obtains Toby for Holmes, and assists in following the trail of the fugitives. Watson continues as Holmes’s practical partner: he observes evidence, pursues leads, reports progress to Mary, represents Holmes while he is absent, receives his telegram, and helps manage Holmes’s disguise. Carrying a stick and later his old service-revolver, Watson joins Holmes and Athelney Jones in the launch pursuit of the Aurora and fires at the Islander, only afterward recognizing how narrowly a dart missed them. After Jonathan Small is captured, Watson delivers the iron treasure box to Mary, opens it, and finds it empty. The central personal change is Watson’s relationship with Mary. Her possible fortune initially makes him confront the selfishness in his feelings, but once the treasure proves empty, he openly declares his love. Mary accepts him as a prospective husband, and Watson believes this may end his role in Holmes’s investigations, despite defending his choice against Holmes’s dissatisfaction.

records.l: Miss Morstan, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Miss Mary Morstan is a young lady, governess, orphan, and daughter of Captain Arthur Morstan. She lives with and works for Mrs. Cecil Forrester in Lower Camberwell, having lived in Edinburgh during childhood. After her father disappears, she receives pearls annually and then an anonymous letter, leading her to seek Sherlock Holmes’s help. She brings a mysterious paper, her father’s preserved Agra plan, and asks Holmes and Dr. Watson to accompany her to a meeting. Though uneasy, she travels with them composedly and resolutely. Thaddeus Sholto reveals that her father died during a quarrel with Major John Sholto and that she is rightfully entitled to at least half of the Agra treasure. She continues to Pondicherry Lodge, comforts the frightened Mrs. Bernstone, and relies on Watson during the frightening events there. Afterward she is exhausted, faints and weeps, yet her chief concern is that Thaddeus be cleared of accusation because he has acted kindly and honourably. She may become an heiress, but the recovered iron treasure box is empty. Its loss removes Watson’s hesitation about declaring his love, and she accepts him as a husband in prospective. Holmes judges her charming and believes her preservation of the Agra plan showed a genius that could have made her useful in investigative work. She becomes a friend of Holmes and Watson and loves Watson reciprocally.
records.t: Miss Mary Morstan is a young lady, governess, orphan, and daughter of Captain Arthur Morstan. She lives with and works for Mrs. Cecil Forrester in Lower Camberwell, having lived in Edinburgh during childhood. After her father disappears, she receives pearls annually and then an anonymous letter, leading her to seek Sherlock Holmes’s help. She brings a mysterious paper—her father’s preserved Agra plan—and asks Holmes and Dr. Watson to accompany her to a meeting. Though uneasy, she travels with them composedly and resolutely. Thaddeus Sholto reveals that her father died during a quarrel with Major John Sholto and that she is rightfully entitled to at least half of the Agra treasure. She continues to Pondicherry Lodge, comforts the frightened Mrs. Bernstone, and relies on Watson during the frightening events there. Afterward she is exhausted, faints and weeps, yet her chief concern is that Thaddeus be cleared of accusation because he has acted kindly and honourably. She may become an heiress, but the recovered iron treasure box is empty. Its loss removes Watson’s hesitation about declaring his love, and she accepts him as a husband in prospective. Holmes judges her charming and believes her preservation of the Agra plan showed a genius that could have made her useful in investigative work. She becomes a friend of Holmes and Watson and loves Watson reciprocally.

records.l: Athelney Jones, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Athelney Jones is a fat, pompous yet well-known, energetic Scotland Yard police detective and inspector. Responsible for investigating the Upper Norwood tragedy and Bartholomew Sholto’s murder, he initially develops the mistaken theory that Thaddeus Sholto killed his brother for the treasure. He arrests Thaddeus, Mrs. Bernstone, Lal Rao, and McMurdo despite evidence of an outside intruder, and Holmes judges his conclusions flawed. After his case against Thaddeus fails, Jones admits the error and asks Sherlock Holmes for help. He accepts Holmes’s direction, supplies a police steam launch and officers, and joins Holmes and Watson in pursuing the Aurora. Though initially doubtful, he helps capture Jonathan Small and the fugitives, takes charge of Small, and ensures the iron treasure box is delivered to Watson. Dismayed to find the box empty, he reproaches Small for frustrating justice. He nevertheless insists on securing Small for trial and receives credit for the investigation, including catching Lal Rao. In relaxation, he is sociable.

records.l: Watson’s elder brother, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Watson’s elder brother, former owner of Watson’s watch, was careless and wasted good prospects, moving between poverty and brief prosperity, repeatedly pawning the watch before dying from drinking.

records.l: the Baker Street Irregulars, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Baker Street Irregulars, dirty and ragged unofficial detectives, arrive at Holmes’s rooms, receive payment to search for the Aurora along both riverbanks and watch Mordecai Smith’s landing-stage, with a guinea promised for finding it.

records.l: Baker Street, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_address_of Sherlock Holmes Baker Street is Holmes’s address and the location where Dr. Watson waits for news. Holmes places it in the advertisement as a contact address, and his telegram directs Athelney Jones to go there.

records.l: Wigmore Street Post-Office, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a post-office [visited by Dr. John Watson] The Wigmore Street Post-Office is identified by Holmes as the place Watson visited earlier that day. Holmes notices reddish earth on Watson’s instep and connects it with pavement work outside the post-office, then deduces that Watson went there to send a telegram.

records.l: The Sign of the Four, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a novel [by Arthur Conan Doyle] The Sign of the Four is the title of the work containing this unit. Its contents list this chapter as Chapter I, “The Science of Deduction.”

records.l: Holmes’s consulting-detective profession, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a profession [specialized in detection] Holmes’s consulting-detective profession involves examining difficult cases referred by official detectives and giving specialist opinions. Holmes says that he created the profession, claims no newspaper credit, and regards the work and the exercise of his powers as their own reward.

records.l: observation and deduction, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a methods of reasoning [observation identifies facts and deduction infers conclusions] Holmes distinguishes observation from deduction: observation reveals details such as reddish earth on Watson’s instep, while deduction connects those details to conclusions such as a visit to the Wigmore Street Post-Office and the sending of a telegram. He says that the ideal detective needs observation, deduction, and knowledge.

records.l: cocaine, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a artificial stimulant [mentally stimulating and clarifying] Cocaine is used by Holmes as a seven-per-cent solution injected with a hypodermic syringe. Holmes considers it mentally stimulating and clarifying, although Watson warns that it may damage the body and produce a severe reaction.

records.l: Watson’s watch, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Watson’s watch, inherited by his elder brother from their father and later in Dr. John Watson’s possession, bears dents, cuts, pawnbroker ticket numbers, and key-hole scratches. Though recently cleaned, Holmes examines it and infers its former owner’s carelessness, financial difficulties, intermittent prosperity, and drunkenness.

records.l: Holmes's telegram, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Holmes’s telegram, sent from Poplar at twelve o’clock, summons Athelney Jones to Baker Street to wait, reporting a close track of the Sholto gang and inviting pursuit that night.

records.l: the cocaine habit, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a habit [recurrent use of cocaine] The cocaine habit is described through Holmes’s repeated injections, which Watson has witnessed three times a day for many months. Watson is increasingly distressed by it, while Holmes says he turns to cocaine when he lacks intellectual work and cannot tolerate mental stagnation.

records.l: the science of deduction, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The science of deduction is presented by Holmes as an exact, unemotional discipline based on analyzing effects and tracing them to causes. Holmes illustrates it by explaining how physical evidence from Watson’s clothing, desk, and watch supports broader conclusions.

records.l: Captain Morstan, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Captain Morstan is an officer in an Indian regiment and its senior captain in 1878. He serves and commands native troops with Major Sholto and Lieutenant Bromley Brown, and is Sholto’s close friend. He possesses curiosities from the Andaman Islands and keeps a mysterious paper bearing a plan, a red cross, a distance note, and references to the sign of the four. In Small’s account, Morstan hears a proposed treasure bargain, goes to Agra, finds the treasure gone, and is said to have betrayed the conspirators with Sholto; he later leaves the army after an inheritance. In 1878 he returns to London on leave, stays at the Langham Hotel, sends for his daughter, and disappears, leaving luggage behind. He had gone to Pondicherry Lodge to claim treasure from Sholto, quarrels with him, suffers a fatal attack, falls, and dies.

records.l: Major Sholto, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Major John Sholto was a British military officer and major of the 34th Bombay Infantry who served in India and at the Andaman Islands. There he commanded native troops with Captain Morstan and Lieutenant Bromley Brown, and he was Morstan’s close friend. After hearing Jonathan Small’s account of hidden treasure, Sholto and Morstan agreed to investigate in return for a share and help for the conspirators. They found the Agra treasure, but Sholto later took it and did not meet the agreed conditions, wronging Small. After retiring from the Indian army, Sholto settled at Pondicherry Lodge in Upper Norwood with his sons, wealth, curiosities, native servants, and the concealed treasure. He hid Morstan’s death and kept Morstan’s share, denying that he had heard Morstan was in London during Morstan’s disappearance. A frightening letter from India made him increasingly fearful, especially of a wooden-legged man, and he fortified and guarded his home with his sons, two prize-fighters, and a khitmutgar. Before dying, he confessed matters concerning Morstan to his sons. He died in bed at Pondicherry Lodge on April 28, 1882; afterward, the Sign of the Four was marked on him, and searches of his papers did not reveal the treasure’s location.

records.l: London, The Sign of the Four
records.s: London is a destination and setting of arrivals, disappearance, investigation, and pursuit. Captain Morstan arrived there in 1878 and vanished; Mary received anonymous messages there. After being repeatedly delayed abroad, the narrator and Tonga reached England and headed toward London. A foggy evening journey crossed its streets and the Thames toward a dubious suburb.

records.l: Langham Hotel, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Langham Hotel was Captain Morstan’s stated address after he returned to London. Mary went there and learned that he had gone out the previous night and had not returned; his luggage remained at the hotel.

records.l: Upper Norwood, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_location_of the Upper Norwood tragedy Upper Norwood is associated with the tragedy involving the Sholtos. The newspaper reports that new evidence cleared Thaddeus Sholto of involvement.

records.l: the Andaman Islands, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Andaman Islands are in the Bay of Bengal, north of Sumatra, contain Port Blair, and are described as home to small, fierce aborigines using clubs and poisoned arrows.

records.l: the Lyceum Theatre, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Lyceum Theatre is the location where the anonymous correspondent instructs Miss Mary Morstan to meet at seven o’clock, at the third pillar from the left. The Lyceum Theatre is the rendezvous where Holmes, Dr. Watson, and Miss Morstan meet a small, dark coachman. The coachman questions Miss Morstan there before arranging their departure in a four-wheeler.

records.l: India, The Sign of the Four
records.s: India is where the narrator served in the army, lost his leg in the Ganges, worked on an indigo plantation, and experienced the Mutiny. He describes the country as being engulfed by fighting, burning, murder, and disorder. India is the setting for the Indian mutiny, the murder and concealment of Achmet’s treasure, and the conspirators’ imprisonment and trials. Major Sholto travels to India to verify Small’s account and takes the treasure from Agra.

records.l: the case, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The case begins with Captain Morstan’s unexplained disappearance, pearls sent annually to Mary, and a promise of justice to a wronged woman. It develops into the locked-room murder of Bartholomew Sholto, the theft of Indian gems, and an investigation of poison, intruders, and escape by the Aurora. Holmes follows physical traces and searches for the fugitives, while Jones suspects Thaddeus. Jonathan Small’s account concludes the case, and Holmes identifies Lal Rao as the confederate in the Norwood affair.

records.l: Captain Morstan's disappearance, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Captain Morstan disappeared in London on 3 December 1878 after leaving the Langham Hotel; inquiries and advertisements found nothing. Holmes linked the disappearance to Major Sholto, the only person Morstan could have visited, and suspected Sholto’s heir knew more. At Pondicherry Lodge, Morstan died after arguing with Major John Sholto over treasure, collapsing and striking his head on a chest. Sholto and Lal Chowdar concealed his body to avoid accusation and disclosure of the treasure.

records.l: the 1878 newspaper advertisement, The Sign of the Four
records.s: After Captain Morstan disappeared, inquiries led to advertisements in the papers, but they produced no result.

records.l: the pearl deliveries, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Beginning about six years before this meeting, a similar box containing a pearl arrived for Miss Mary Morstan every year on the same date. No writing or clue identifying the sender accompanied the deliveries.

records.l: pearls sent to Mary Morstan, The Sign of the Four
records.s: are rare and valuable [pronounced so by an expert] The pearls sent to Mary Morstan are described as very large, lustrous, and handsome. An expert pronounced them to be of a rare variety and considerable value.

records.l: pearl boxes sent to Mary Morstan, The Sign of the Four
records.s: contain pearls sent to Mary Morstan [one similar pearl in each box] The pearl boxes were small cardboard boxes addressed to Miss Mary Morstan. Each contained a pearl, and Holmes examines the writing on their addresses for comparison with the anonymous letter.

records.l: the anonymous letter, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The anonymous letter, signed without a name, summons Captain Morstan’s daughter Mary to the third pillar outside the Lyceum Theatre at seven o’clock. It promises justice for her as a wronged woman, forbids police, permits two friends, and is linked by Holmes to presents received after Major Sholto’s death.

records.l: the anonymous correspondent, The Sign of the Four
records.s: promises justice [to Miss Mary Morstan] The anonymous correspondent sends Mary annual pearls and writes the letter arranging the Lyceum Theatre meeting. The correspondent’s identity is unknown, but Holmes concludes that the same person wrote the letter and the pearl-box addresses.

records.l: the handwriting, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The anonymous correspondent’s disguised handwriting appears on pearl-box addresses and an anonymous letter, identified as shared through an irrepressible Greek e and recurring final-s twirl.

records.l: the meeting at the Lyceum Theatre, The Sign of the Four
records.s: A meeting at the Lyceum Theatre is arranged for seven o’clock at the third pillar from the left, where Miss Mary Morstan, Sherlock Holmes, and Dr. John Watson are to attend without police.

records.l: the investigation, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The investigation concerns Mary Morstan, beginning with Holmes recording Captain Morstan’s disappearance and examining correspondence before a Lyceum Theatre meeting. It matters as the narrator expects it may be his last case with Holmes because of marriage; it ends with them comparing their contributions and outcomes.

records.l: Jonathan Small, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Jonathan Small is a middle-aged, sunburned, bearded former convict with a wooden right leg, a scarred hand, black curly hair shot with grey, and a reckless, heavily lined appearance. Poorly educated but cunning, he is one of four associates connected by the Agra treasure: Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, and Dost Akbar. He participated with them in Achmet’s murder, received a life sentence of penal servitude after a death sentence was commuted, and was transferred via Madras to the Andaman convict-barracks. There he served alongside the other three men, behaved well enough to gain privileges, learned some medicine while dispensing drugs, and came to regard the treasure as earned through twenty years of suffering, though useless if he could not possess it. Seeking freedom and vengeance, Small made a bargain with Major Sholto and Captain Morstan: a fifth share of the treasure in exchange for the conspirators’ release. The treasure was instead stolen from him, giving him reason to pursue the Sholtos and maintain watch over Pondicherry Lodge. He escaped the Andamans with Tonga after killing a convict-guard, using passages he arranged toward America or the Colonies. Holmes identifies him as the wooden-legged man linked to Captain Morstan’s chart, the removal of the treasure-box, and the search for revenge. Small says Tonga, not he, killed Thaddeus Sholto with a poisoned dart. While preparing to flee with the treasure, Small has Mordecai Smith hide the Aurora at Jacobson’s Yard and directs the launch during the Thames pursuit. The launch runs onto the southern bank; his wooden leg leaves him stuck in mud, and he is captured. In custody, he claims nearly half a million pounds from the treasure, says he acted for all four imprisoned men, and agrees to tell his story. He has hidden or discarded the treasure so that neither authorities nor the Sholto and Morstan families can recover it. After explaining that he brought the rope and that Tonga had only one dart left, he is taken away under guard by Athelney Jones.

records.l: Mahomet Singh, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Mahomet Singh is a tall, great black-bearded Sikh trooper under the narrator’s command and an old fighting-man who fought at Chilian-wallah. One of three Sikh conspirators, he helps Abdullah Khan threaten the narrator and is assigned to watch for Dost Akbar and Achmet. He pursues a fat man through a passage with a flashing knife and stabs him after the man falls. Later he helps carry Achmet’s body into the fort, guards the door, and joins the conspirators in concealing treasure, swearing oaths, making charts, and negotiating with Major Sholto and Captain Morstan.

records.l: Abdullah Khan, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Abdullah Khan is a fierce Sikh trooper, an old fighting-man who fought at Chilian-wallah, and one of three Sikh conspirators. He threatens the narrator into joining a plot to seize Achmet and divide the rajah’s jewels, escorts Achmet, helps carry his body into Agra fort and conceal the treasure, swears unity with the four conspirators, and later negotiates with Major Sholto and Captain Morstan.

records.l: Dost Akbar, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Dost Akbar, a Sikh and Abdullah Khan’s foster-brother, knows Achmet’s secret and is expected to guide him to an isolated gate for a share of treasure. He helps carry Achmet’s body into the fort, swears with the conspirators, and joins their bargain with Major Sholto and Captain Morstan.

records.l: the Thames, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Thames is a river with many wharves and landing-places on both sides, especially below the bridge. Toby’s trail brings Holmes and Watson to its edge, where fugitives are thought to have boarded a boat. Searches on both sides fail, and Holmes goes downstream in disguise. It becomes the route of the Aurora’s rapid pursuit past bridges, docks, and marshes; the Islander falls into its dark ooze, and Jonathan Small throws away the treasure-box key.

records.l: the mystery, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The mystery initially appears to Holmes to have one explanation connecting Captain Morstan’s disappearance, Major Sholto’s death, and the presents sent to Miss Morstan. The mysterious paper introduces further complications, causing Holmes to reconsider his ideas.

records.l: the night’s expedition, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The night’s expedition is a secret journey by Sherlock Holmes, Dr. Watson, and Miss Morstan to resolve the mystery, traveling through foggy London to a dark suburban house.

records.l: Major Sholto’s death, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Major Sholto’s death, on April 28, 1882, followed a confession to his sons that he had concealed Captain Morstan’s death and kept Morstan’s treasure share. As he began to disclose the treasure’s location, a bearded face appeared at the window; he cried out and died before the narrator arrived. His papers revealed nothing, and Morstan’s daughter soon began receiving yearly valuable presents.

records.l: the mysterious paper, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The mysterious paper is a native Indian document, apparently once pinned to a board, found carefully kept in Captain Morstan’s pocket-book. It shows a plan of part of a large building with halls, corridors, and passages, marked by a red cross, “3.37 from left,” and the sign of the four. Holmes deems it important and asks Miss Morstan to preserve it.

records.l: the sign of the four, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The sign of the four is an inscription and identifying mark used by Jonathan Small with Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, and Dost Akbar. It first appears as a hieroglyphic of four touching crosses on a mysterious paper and on Captain Morstan’s chart. Later, its words are scrawled on torn note-paper beside Bartholomew Sholto’s body, where Holmes treats it as significant murder evidence.

records.l: the four-wheeler, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_driven_by the coachman [during the journey] A four-wheeler brings Miss Morstan to the Lyceum Theatre and later carries her, Sherlock Holmes, and Dr. Watson through the foggy streets. A coachman drives it at a furious pace to an unknown destination, eventually stopping at a new suburban terrace.

records.l: Thaddeus Sholto, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Thaddeus Sholto is a small, thirty-year-old, wealthy man with a bald shining scalp fringed by red hair, a confirmed hypochondriac, and the twin son of Major John Sholto. He is Bartholomew Sholto’s brother, lives in the Sholto apartment after leaving Pondicherry Lodge, and uses a hookah as a sedative. As an heir entitled to half the Agra treasure, he seeks an inheritance claim for Miss Morstan and himself. He invites Miss Morstan, Sherlock Holmes, and Dr. Watson to hear the history of Major John Sholto, Captain Arthur Morstan, and the treasure, explains that he sent Miss Morstan pearls, and leads them to Pondicherry Lodge to claim her share. There he fears Bartholomew’s silence, admits helping lower the treasure, and reports the death. Suspected because of a quarrel and his earlier presence, he is arrested but later released and cleared by an unshaken alibi. A later record says he is killed by Tonga’s poisoned dart, though Jonathan Small says Sholto was already dead when he entered.

records.l: Bartholomew Sholto, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Bartholomew Sholto is the clever twin brother of Thaddeus Sholto and one of Major John Sholto’s two sons. Favoured by his father according to Thaddeus, he is a master of Pondicherry Lodge and has a chamber fitted as a chemical laboratory. Angry with Thaddeus for contacting Miss Morstan, he discovers the hidden treasure by noticing four unaccounted-for feet in the house’s height and finding a sealed garret. He possesses the stolen Indian gems inherited from his father and keeps the recovered treasure in his laboratory. There, after the treasure’s discovery, an unnamed associate of Jonathan Small enters through the roof; Tonga kills Bartholomew during the theft. He is found many hours dead in the locked laboratory, seated stiff and cold with contracted limbs, a distorted face and fixed smile, and a poisoned thorn above his ear. The poison is a powerful vegetable alkaloid delivered through a ceiling hole.

records.l: Pondicherry Lodge, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Pondicherry Lodge is Major John Sholto’s large, square home in Upper Norwood, where he lived luxuriously with his sons and native servants and where Captain Morstan died. Enclosed by desolate grounds, a high glass-topped wall, and a single guarded entrance, it is gloomy, silent, and marked by treasure-seekers’ excavations. Its sealed garret above the highest room held hidden treasure. After Bartholomew discovers it, he dies in a locked room; police, investigators, Sherlock Holmes, and Dr. John Watson examine the house, garret, roof, and grounds, beginning a pursuit. It remains guarded afterward, while later news reports continued treasure searches and eventually its discovery.

records.l: Norwood, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Norwood is where Pondicherry Lodge is located. Thaddeus Sholto says that the party must travel there to meet Bartholomew Sholto and demand Miss Morstan’s share of the treasure.

records.l: the Agra treasure, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Agra treasure is a valuable collection of Indian gems, estimated at nearly or at least half a million pounds. It includes diamonds, emeralds, rubies, carbuncles, sapphires, agates, beryls, onyxes, cats’-eyes, turquoises, pearls, the Great Mogul diamond, and a gold coronet set with twelve pearls. Four conspirators originally hide it beneath bricks in a preserved wall of the Agra fort. Major John Sholto and Captain Arthur Morstan acquire it in India, but Major Sholto betrays the agreement, takes it, and brings it to England, where he possesses it for years. At Pondicherry Lodge, Bartholomew Sholto discovers the treasure in a sealed garret or secret room. Soon after it is lowered through an opening in the ceiling, it vanishes from Bartholomew’s chamber. Its disappearance, followed by Bartholomew’s murder, leads Athelney Jones to suspect Thaddeus Sholto, while Sherlock Holmes attributes it to intruders and believes Jonathan Small came to regain what he considered his rights. The fugitives are thought to have carried away the box, and recovery matters especially because Miss Morstan is entitled to half, with the other half to go to Thaddeus Sholto. The recovered box proves empty. Jonathan Small says the treasure has brought murder, fear, guilt, and slavery, calls it cursed, and states that he placed it beyond recovery, possibly scattering it over several miles in the Thames. Thus the treasure ends lost despite its recovery being sought for six years.

records.l: Morstan’s share of the treasure, The Sign of the Four
records.s: belongs_to Miss Morstan [as her rightful inheritance] Morstan’s share of the treasure was owed to Miss Morstan, but Major John Sholto concealed it along with the body and kept it despite making no use of it. Thaddeus Sholto says that he and Bartholomew must make restitution, and he travels with Miss Morstan to pursue the claim.

records.l: the torn paper bearing The sign of the four, The Sign of the Four
records.s: was_found_at Pondicherry Lodge [fixed upon Major Sholto’s chest] After Major Sholto’s death, his room was found disturbed and a torn piece of paper bearing the words “The sign of the four” was fixed to his chest. The meaning of the phrase and the identity of the visitor connected with it remained unknown to Thaddeus and Bartholomew.

records.l: the discovery of the treasure, The Sign of the Four
records.s: occurred_at Pondicherry Lodge [after Bartholomew Sholto found the sealed garret] Bartholomew Sholto discovered the treasure by measuring the house and finding four feet of height unaccounted for. He opened the ceiling of the highest room and found a sealed garret containing the treasure-chest.

records.l: the inheritance claim, The Sign of the Four
records.s: concerns Morstan’s share of the treasure [to be demanded from Bartholomew Sholto] The inheritance claim concerns Miss Morstan’s right to at least half of the Agra treasure, which Major John Sholto had withheld. Thaddeus Sholto intends to accompany her to Pondicherry Lodge and demand her share from Bartholomew Sholto.

records.l: the treasure hunt, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The treasure hunt, conducted by the Sholtos and people connected with Pondicherry Lodge, lasted six years and ended when the treasure was found in Bartholomew Sholto's chemical laboratory.

records.l: the murder of Bartholomew Sholto, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The murder of Bartholomew Sholto occurred at Pondicherry Lodge in Upper Norwood during the theft of the treasure. Holmes identified the locked-room death as murder after finding a poisoned thorn, unusual hammer-like instrument, torn note, ceiling opening, and missing treasure. He attributed the extreme contraction and risus sardonicus to a powerful vegetable alkaloid, like strychnine, delivered by the thorn. Footprints, weapons, a card linked to Captain Morstan’s chart, and poison led Holmes to conclude that Jonathan Small’s unnamed associate killed Bartholomew while Small removed the treasure-box. A newspaper reported arrests and falsely credited Athelney Jones; later, Tonga was said to have killed him after entering through the roof.

records.l: the poisoned thorn, The Sign of the Four
records.s: A long, dark, black thorn, not an English thorn, is driven or shot through a ceiling opening into Bartholomew Sholto’s scalp above his ear. Its pointed end bears dried gummy poison, apparently causing fatal poisoning. Holmes warns of it, and Watson removes it, leaving a tiny speck of blood.

records.l: the chemical laboratory at Pondicherry Lodge, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The chemical laboratory at the top of Pondicherry Lodge is the upper secret chamber where the treasure was found. Bare and dusty, with rafter flooring, no furniture, small naked footprints, and a trap-door to the roof, it later matters as the planned route for Tonga's entry.

records.l: the rope, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The rope enables Jonathan Small to climb and descend through a window, leaving blood marks after he slips and injures his hand. Later, wound around Tonga’s waist and secured for access through a laboratory roof, it helps the narrator climb, lowers the treasure-box, and is pulled up as Tonga escapes.

records.l: the Islander, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Islander is Jonathan Small’s able, efficient ally and Andaman islander: a small black dwarf with a greatly misshapen head and features marked by bestiality and cruelty. Savage and violent, he carries a stone-headed wooden mace, a blowpipe, and poisoned darts or poison spines. He enters through a roof trap-door and helps Jonathan Small enter and leave a secret room by managing a rope, hook, and window. Able to reach a lofty garret inaccessible to Jonathan Small, he enters Bartholomew Sholto’s room, kills him with poison, and leaves creosote-marked bare footprints. During pursuit, wrapped in a dark ulster or blanket, he threatens the pursuers with a short wooden weapon, falls overboard, and dies in the Thames.

records.l: Toby, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Toby is a queer mongrel dog, ugly, long-haired, lop-eared, brown-and-white, and half spaniel and half lurcher. Owned or kept by Mr. Sherman at No. 7 Pinchin Lane, he has an extraordinary sense of smell and is used to track scents. Holmes obtains Toby to follow a creasote trail left by Jonathan Small and his associate. Toby tracks it from Pondicherry Lodge through London, eagerly leading Holmes and the narrator into a timber-yard. When crossed trails mislead him, he is returned to the confusion point, finds the true route toward the river, and is kept by Holmes for possible future use.

records.l: the arrest of Thaddeus Sholto, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_based_on the murder investigation [Athelney Jones’s theory] Athelney Jones arrests Thaddeus Sholto in the Queen’s name for being concerned in the death of his brother. Holmes immediately tells Thaddeus not to worry and says he expects to clear him.

records.l: the theft of the treasure, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The theft of the treasure is carried out by the narrator and Tonga, who enter the chemical laboratory through a roof trap-door, take the treasure-box, lower it by rope, and escape. The jewels are missing from the locked house; the sign of the four is left behind, and Holmes attributes the crime to the intruders.

records.l: the rajah's treasure, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The rajah’s treasure consists of precious stones and choice pearls placed in an iron box and sent to Agra for safekeeping. Abdullah Khan proposed dividing it among himself, Mahomet Singh, Dost Akbar, and the narrator. Years later it was found in the chemical laboratory at Pondicherry Lodge, then taken at night toward a ship; after Bartholomew Sholto’s death, it was missing and central to Jones’s accusation against Thaddeus Sholto.

records.l: the narrator's wooden leg, The Sign of the Four
records.s: belongs_to Jonathan Small [serving as his right leg] The wooden stump leaves circular muddy impressions on the sill, floor, and near the table. Holmes uses these marks to establish that a wooden-legged man entered through the window.

records.l: creosote, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Creosote is a dark liquid with a pungent, heavy tracking scent. It leaks from a cracked carboy, pervades the room, is stepped in to leave a small footprint, and is identified around a barrel and trolley so Holmes can have Toby follow its powerful smell.

records.l: the trap-door in the roof, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The trap-door connects the secret room’s garret to the roof, provides access to the chemical laboratory, and is evidence in conflicting conclusions about an ally’s entry and an escape.

records.l: the footprints, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Footprints and impressions include a heavy boot print, circular wooden-stump marks near the window and inside, and many small naked-foot prints in the secret room, tracing intruders’ movements.

records.l: the poison, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The poison produces extreme muscular contraction, a distorted face, and risus sardonicus. Dr. Watson and Holmes identify it as a powerful vegetable alkaloid resembling strychnine and causing tetanus.

records.l: Jonathan Small’s associates, The Sign of the Four
records.s: are convicts [unable to escape and obtain the treasure] Jonathan Small’s associates were convicts who could not obtain the treasure when Captain Morstan’s chart was made. The chart identifies Jonathan Small and his associates as the four connected with the treasure.

records.l: the Andamans, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Andamans are a remote, fever-stricken penal settlement hundreds of miles from other land, making escape difficult. Small eventually escapes from there with Tonga by canoe.

records.l: the Agra treasure mystery, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Agra treasure mystery leads from Captain Morstan’s death and the pearls to the chart, Major Sholto’s death, the treasure’s rediscovery, and Bartholomew Sholto’s murder. Sherlock Holmes develops a reconstruction involving Jonathan Small and his unnamed associate.

records.l: the pursuit of Jonathan Small and his associate, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. John Watson pursue Jonathan Small and his associate, beginning at Pondicherry Lodge as Toby follows their creasote scent across London.

records.l: Captain Morstan’s chart, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Captain Morstan’s chart, signed by Jonathan Small for himself and his associates as the Sign of the Four, lets Sherlock Holmes connect them to the buried treasure.

records.l: the poison spines, The Sign of the Four
records.s: are dark wooden spines [sharp at one end and rounded at the other] The poison spines are dark wooden, sharply pointed objects found in a small woven pouch dropped during the escape. Sherlock Holmes identifies them as like the weapon that struck Bartholomew Sholto and warns Dr. John Watson not to prick himself.

records.l: the creasote trail, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_created_by the unnamed associate of Jonathan Small [by stepping in creasote] The creasote trail was left when the unnamed associate placed a bare foot in creasote while escaping through the garret window. Sherlock Holmes uses the scent on a handkerchief to direct Toby, whose nose follows it despite the traffic on the London road.

records.l: Broderick and Nelson’s large timber-yard, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Broderick and Nelson’s large timber-yard, just past the White Eagle tavern on Nine Elms, unfolds as Toby enters through a side-gate and runs through it to a barrel on a hand-trolley.

records.l: the creasote barrel, The Sign of the Four
records.s: A large cask of creosote-smeared staves is brought to the timber-yard on a hand-trolley, where it stands as Toby springs onto it with a triumphant yelp.

records.l: Mordecai Smith, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Mordecai Smith is a boatman, husband of Mrs. Smith, and father of Jim Smith. He owns the steam launch Aurora and hires out boats from Smith’s Wharf and landing-stage. After a wooden-legged man rouses him at night, he leaves with Jim in the Aurora and disappears, prompting Holmes’s advertisement. Holmes later finds him at Jacobson’s Yard; Smith takes two gentlemen aboard, shovels coal during a chase, and finally submits with Jim.

records.l: the wooden-legged man, The Sign of the Four
records.s: A brown, monkey-faced man with a wooden leg, associated with Jonathan Small, visits Mrs. Smith at night and departs with Smith in the Aurora.

records.l: Wiggins, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Wiggins, senior leader of the Baker Street Irregulars, receives Holmes’s telegraph, gathers them at Baker Street, and manages their reports during the Aurora search.

records.l: the Aurora, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Aurora is Mordecai Smith’s black steam launch, marked by two red streaks or stripes and a black funnel with a white band. Known as a fast “clipper” and one of the river’s fastest launches, it is engaged from old Smith to carry Jonathan Small and Tonga to their ship as an escape vessel. Smith, his son Jim, Small, and the Islander take it down the River Thames after it leaves Smith’s Wharf early Tuesday, prompting a missing-launch investigation and Holmes’s search. A wooden-legged man briefly places it at Jacobson’s Yard for a rudder alteration. It then departs at high speed, making pursuit difficult, but eventually runs aground and is captured by Holmes’s party.

records.l: Mordecai Smith's boats and landing-stage, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_departure_point_for steam launch Aurora Smith’s Wharf is the place from which Mordecai Smith and his son Jim departed in the Aurora. The advertisement directs anyone with information to contact Mrs. Smith there.

records.l: the steam launch chase, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The chase leads Holmes and Watson from the recovered scent to Mordecai Smith’s landing-stage and the missing Aurora. Rather than search every wharf themselves or alert the police and fugitives, Holmes employs the Baker Street Irregulars to watch both banks and await news.

records.l: the Sholto gang, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_pursued_by Sherlock Holmes [in connection with the treasure] Holmes’s telegram states that he is close on the track of the Sholto gang. He plans to give Athelney Jones two new prisoners in place of the released suspects.

records.l: Westminster Stairs, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_departure_point_for the police-boat [at seven o’clock] Westminster Stairs is the meeting point where Holmes requires a fast police steam launch to be at seven o’clock.

records.l: the Sholtos' treasure, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Sholtos’ treasure is a massive, solid iron chest of Indian workmanship, made of Benares metal-work and associated with the rajah’s and Agra treasures: precious stones and choice pearls. Conspirators open it with a key hung by a silken cord from its carved handle, inventory the jewels, replace them, and hide the chest beneath bricks in a sound wall of the Agra fort. Later it is carried by Achmet in a shawl-wrapped bundle, said to contain only family matters, though others believe it holds the rajah’s jewels. The box is taken from a chemical laboratory, and eventually found aboard the Aurora. Its key has been thrown into the Thames, so Dr. Watson forces it open for Mary Morstan; despite its thick iron construction, it is empty.

records.l: the advertisement, The Sign of the Four
records.s: offers_reward five pounds [for information about Mordecai Smith and the launch] The advertisement offers five pounds for information about Mordecai Smith, his son Jim, and the Aurora. It is placed at Mrs. Smith’s address and at Baker Street so the fugitives might read it as an ordinary message from a worried wife.

records.l: Holmes's disguise, The Sign of the Four
records.s: includes the old sailor disguise Holmes uses a simple disguise because members of the criminal classes are beginning to recognize him. He works all day in the disguise while pursuing information about the missing launch and the fugitives.

records.l: the old sailor disguise, The Sign of the Four
records.s: depicts an aged seafaring man [with a pea-jacket and coloured scarf] The old sailor disguise consists of a wig, white whiskers and eyebrows, a pea-jacket, a coloured scarf, a cudgel, and an affected aged and asthmatic manner. Holmes uses it to enter Baker Street as an apparently impoverished master mariner carrying information, then reveals himself.

records.l: the Upper Norwood tragedy, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_subject_of the inquest [scheduled for the following day] The Upper Norwood tragedy is reported in the newspapers, which had initially treated Thaddeus Sholto as a suspect. Fresh evidence establishes that Sholto could not have been involved, and he is released.

records.l: the search for the fugitives, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The search for the fugitives is delayed because no trace of the Aurora or the missing men can be found. Holmes uses other agencies, an advertisement, river searches, and a disguise before arranging a police-boat pursuit.

records.l: the missing-launch investigation, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The missing-launch investigation concerns Mordecai Smith, his son Jim, and the Aurora, which disappeared after leaving Smith’s Wharf. Despite searches along the river and inquiries with Mrs. Smith, no immediate news is obtained until Holmes develops a new lead.

records.l: Sherlock Holmes's launch, The Sign of the Four
records.s: A very fast police-boat, its green identifying lamp removed, carries Holmes, Watson, Jones, police workers, and the Sholtos' treasure. It pursues the Aurora down the Thames, catches it near marshes, frees it from a bank, and tows it upstream.

records.l: Jacobson's Yard, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Jacobson's Yard conceals the Aurora after Jonathan Small arranges for a minor change to its rudder. Holmes discovers the launch there and places a boy nearby to signal when it departs.

records.l: the Sholtos, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Sholtos are connected to the iron chest recovered from the Aurora, which Holmes identifies as the chest that contained their ill-omened treasure.

records.l: the pursuit and capture of Jonathan Small, The Sign of the Four
records.s: A high-speed Thames man-hunt in which Holmes, Athelney Jones, and companions chase Jonathan Small's Aurora after it leaves Jacobson's Yard. Their launch fights through heavy traffic and gradually gains until the Aurora runs onto a muddy bank. The pursuers seize the Aurora, capture Small and the Smiths, and take Small to Baker Street; the approaching launch prevents him from keeping the treasure as he tries to reach the Esmeralda at Gravesend.

records.l: the Islander's death, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_caused_by the Thames [the Islander falls into the river] The Islander is shot after he draws a short wooden weapon and raises it to his lips. He falls into the Thames, and although the pursuers search with their light, they find no sign of him; the text states that his bones lie at the bottom of the river.

records.l: Tonga, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Tonga is an Andaman Islander and devoted companion of Small. Small nurses him back to health, and Tonga helps him escape the island in his large canoe with supplies; they sail together for ten days before a trader rescues them. Tonga later travels with the narrator and is exhibited at fairs as a black cannibal, eating raw meat and performing a war-dance. During the theft of the treasure, he climbs into the chemical laboratory, kills Bartholomew Sholto, shoots Thaddeus Sholto with a poisoned dart, helps move the treasure-box, and escapes, leaving clues that help Holmes track him.

records.l: Achmet, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Achmet is a fat, trusted merchant of the rajah, traveling with Dost Akbar and carrying an iron box of jewels and pearls. Frightened, he seeks protection in the Agra fort. Although the narrator orders him taken to the main guard, Achmet runs through the corridors bloodied and pursued by a Sikh. The narrator trips him with a firelock, and the Sikh stabs him twice. Achmet is buried under loose bricks; his disappearance is later discovered when a spy reports his entry into the fort.

records.l: the murder of Thaddeus Sholto, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_caused_by Tonga's poisoned darts [according to Jonathan Small] The murder of Thaddeus Sholto is attributed by Jonathan Small to Tonga, who fired a poisoned dart. Small denies committing the killing, and Holmes believes Sholto died before Small entered the room.

records.l: the treasure's loss, The Sign of the Four
records.s: removes_barrier_between Watson and Mary Morstan's love [the fortune no longer separates them] The treasure's loss is discovered when Dr. Watson and Mary Morstan open the iron box and find it completely empty. The loss removes what Watson sees as a barrier between him and Mary, allowing him to confess his love.

records.l: Watson and Mary Morstan's love, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_gained_through the treasure's loss [after the treasure is found to be gone] When the treasure is found to be gone, Dr. Watson tells Mary Morstan that he loves her and that the riches had sealed his lips. Mary does not withdraw her hand and whispers that she also says, "Thank God," as they come together.

records.l: the empty box, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a container without the treasure The empty box is shown to the inspector and then to Athelney Jones after the pursuit. Its emptiness reveals that Jonathan Small removed the treasure before the authorities could capture him.

records.l: Jonathan Small's trial, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_affected_by Jonathan Small's cooperation with justice [his chances would improve if he helped justice] Jonathan Small is to be taken into custody, and Holmes and the narrator are expected to appear at the trial.

records.l: justice, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_rejected_by Jonathan Small [he regards it as unfair in this matter] Athelney Jones claims that Small has thwarted justice by withholding the treasure. Small rejects this idea, arguing that it is unjust for people who did not earn the treasure to enjoy it, while Holmes says justice cannot be assessed until Small’s account is heard.

records.l: the unnamed narrator, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The unnamed narrator is a Worcestershire man, born near Pershore and born into the Smalls family. A youthful rover, he joins the 3rd Buffs after trouble over a girl, serves in India, and loses his right leg above the knee to a crocodile in the Ganges. Invalided out, he becomes Abel White’s plantation overseer, survives the Mutiny, and joins Agra’s volunteer corps. While commanding a postern gate, he agrees to rob and kill Achmet for treasure, but ultimately sends Achmet to the main guard.

records.l: Abel White, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Abel White, a kind Worcestershire-born indigo-planter in India, owned a plantation at Muttra and employed the narrator as overseer; during the Mutiny, rebels attacked and burned his bungalow.

records.l: the Indian Mutiny, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a great mutiny [throughout India] The Indian Mutiny suddenly spread across the country after a period of apparent peace. It left Europeans fleeing toward places such as Agra and brought widespread fighting, torture, murder, and outrage.

records.l: Agra, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Agra is a city and place of refuge for Europeans fleeing disturbances around Muttra, though it is filled with fanatics and fierce groups as British defenders concentrate in the old fort. It is also where Achmet is murdered, treasure is hidden and found by Major Sholto, and conspirators are tried.

records.l: the British, The Sign of the Four
records.s: hold the ground that their guns commanded [in small bands during the uprising] The British in the region were reduced to small groups holding only the ground commanded by their guns. At Agra, soldiers, volunteers, women, children, and stores were gathered inside the fort.

records.l: the rebel army, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_composed_of the Sepoys [among its forces] The rebel army was made up of forces opposing the British during the Mutiny. Abdullah Khan planned to pass over to the rebels if the conspiracy at the gate failed.

records.l: the Sepoys, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Sepoys were described as the British-trained troops who had turned against them, using British weapons and bugle-calls. Four Sepoys were found dead near Dawson, and many others were among the rebels surrounding Abel White’s bungalow.

records.l: the Sikh friends, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_stationed_at Agra [during the mutiny] Sikh troops formed part of the forces defending Agra and included the two Sikh troopers assigned to the narrator. The two men under his command were Mahomet Singh and Abdullah Khan, both experienced fighters.

records.l: the Agra Fort, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Agra Fort, in Agra, has a central guard-house and a small isolated postern gate on its southwest side. It contains a modern occupied section and a larger deserted quarter of halls, passages, and corridors, with gates guarded by small detachments. Conspirators carry Achmet’s body to a crumbling hall and conceal a treasure chest beneath bricks in a best-preserved wall.

records.l: the rajah, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The rajah of the northern provinces amassed inherited and hoarded treasure, dividing gold and silver in his palace from jewels secretly sent to Agra. After supporting the Sepoys, he was deposed and driven out of India; conspirators treated his property as loot.

records.l: the postern gate, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The postern gate was a small isolated door on the southwest side of the Agra Fort. The narrator guarded it with Mahomet Singh and Abdullah Khan, and Dost Akbar chose it as the entry point for Achmet.

records.l: the conspiracy to rob Achmet, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Abdullah Khan, with Mahomet Singh and Dost Akbar, planned to admit Achmet into the fort, kill him, hide his disappearance, and seize the rajah’s jewels; despite being forced to swear noninterference, the narrator had Achmet taken to the main guard.

records.l: long, straight passage, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a passage [long and straight] The long, straight passage is where the narrator sees the fat man running toward him, with the Sikh close behind. It leads toward the open air.

records.l: firelock, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_used_as obstacle [placed between the fat man's legs] The narrator casts the firelock between the fat man's legs as he runs past. The fat man trips over it and rolls twice over.

records.l: knife, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The Sikh carries a knife that flashes in his hand. He uses it to stab the fat man twice in the side.

records.l: fat man's flight, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_toward open air [if he passed the speaker] The fat man runs extremely fast through the passage, with the Sikh close behind him. He is gaining on the Sikh and might have saved himself by reaching the open air, but the narrator stops him.

records.l: fat man's fall, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The firelock catches the fat man's legs, causing him to roll twice over like a shot rabbit. He may have broken his neck in the fall.

records.l: stabbing of the fat man, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_performed_with knife [twice in his side] After the fat man falls, the Sikh buries his knife twice in the man's side. The fat man never utters a moan or moves a muscle and remains where he fell.

records.l: the four treasure conspirators, The Sign of the Four
records.s: The four treasure conspirators are Small, Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, and Dost Akbar. They jointly possess and claim entitlement to the Agra treasure, represented by their shared sign. They murder and bury Achmet, conceal his jewels in the Agra fort, swear to act together, and are arrested and sentenced for murder. Later they offer the treasure’s location for freedom; their sign is left on Major Sholto and in the chemical laboratory to assert their claim.

records.l: the murder of Achmet, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_a murder [of Achmet the merchant] The murder of Achmet is committed by the four treasure conspirators after Achmet enters the fort with the rajah’s jewels. His body is hidden in a crumbling hall, but a spy’s report leads to its discovery and the arrest and trial of the conspirators.

records.l: Small's escape from the Andamans, The Sign of the Four
records.s: Small escapes the Andamans with Tonga by canoe after arranging supplies and a nighttime departure. Before leaving, he kills a convict-guard who repeatedly mistreated him; using a bamboo spear and coconut-matting sail, they reach a trader from Singapore to Jiddah.

records.l: the treasure plans, The Sign of the Four
records.s: are_created_for the four treasure conspirators [one plan for each conspirator] Small draws four plans marking the treasure’s hiding place, one for each conspirator, and marks them with the sign of the four. He later prepares two additional charts for Major Sholto and Captain Morstan, identifying the relevant part of the Agra fort and signing them with the same sign.

records.l: Blair Island, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is_part_of the Andamans [penal settlement] Blair Island in the Andamans is the settlement to which Small is transferred after serving time at Agra and Madras. Small lives at Hope Town on Mount Harriet, performs labor, learns to dispense drugs, and looks for a way to escape.

records.l: the conspiracy's oath, The Sign of the Four
records.s: requires collective_action [the four conspirators must act together] The conspirators’ oath binds them to stand by one another, keep the treasure secret, and act together so that none can take advantage. Small insists that any escape bargain must include all four conspirators because of this oath.

records.l: the treasure bargain, The Sign of the Four
records.s: offers a fifth share [to Major Sholto and Captain Morstan jointly] Small offers Major Sholto and Captain Morstan a share of the treasure in exchange for freeing all four conspirators and providing a yacht, provisions, and passage to the Indian coast. The officers agree to investigate, but Sholto takes the treasure and fails to carry out the agreed conditions.

records.l: the escape by the Aurora, The Sign of the Four
records.s: uses the launch Aurora [to reach the ship] The narrator arranged to use old Smith's launch Aurora to escape with Tonga and reach their ship. Smith was promised a large sum for getting them there safely, though he was not told their secrets.

records.l: the narrator's innocence, The Sign of the Four
records.s: concerns Bartholomew Sholto's killing [as asserted by the narrator] The narrator claims that he is innocent of Bartholomew Sholto's death because Tonga killed him. He presents his account as the truth and says he is revealing everything because he believes this is his best defense.

records.l: the prospective marriage of the narrator and Miss Morstan, The Sign of the Four
records.s: is accepted by Miss Morstan [as a marriage prospect] Miss Morstan has accepted the narrator as a husband in prospective. The narrator expects the marriage to affect his future participation in investigations with Holmes, while Holmes says that emotional attachments conflict with the cold reason he values.

records.l: the cocaine-bottle, The Sign of the Four
records.s: After the case, the narrator says that he receives a wife and Jones receives the credit, and asks what remains for Holmes. Holmes answers that the cocaine-bottle remains for him and reaches for it.

records.l: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
records.s: Hatty Doran has character wild, free, impetuous, fearless, and noble
records.q: She is what we call in England a tomboy, with a strong nature, wild and free, unfettered by any sort of traditions. She is impetuous—volcanic, I was about to say. She is swift in making up her mind and fearless in carrying out her resolutions. On the other hand, I would not have given her the name which I have the honour to bear”—he gave a little stately cough—“had I not thought her to be at bottom a noble woman.

records.q: He takes the obvious course of keeping her at home and forbidding her to seek the company of people of her own age. But soon he found that that would not answer forever. She became restive, insisted upon her rights, and finally announced her positive intention of going to a certain ball. What does her clever stepfather do then? He conceives an idea more creditable to his head than to his heart. With the connivance and assistance of his wife he disguised himself, covered those keen eyes with tinted glasses, masked the face with a moustache and a pair of bushy whiskers, sunk that clear voice into an insinuating whisper, and doubly secure on account of the girl’s short sight, he appears as Mr. Hosmer Angel, and keeps off other lovers by making love himself.

records.l: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: Sherlock Holmes reunites with Dr. Watson at Baker Street and receives an invitation note warning that a masked visitor will consult him. The visitor is Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, hereditary King of Bohemia, who reveals that Irene Adler possesses a compromising photograph of them together. The King wants Holmes to recover the photograph before Irene sends it to the family of his intended bride, Clotilde Lothman von Saxe-Meningen. Holmes accepts the case, receives Irene Adler’s address at Briony Lodge, and is given carte blanche and funds for expenses.

records.l: Sherlock Holmes, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: Sherlock Holmes is consulted by Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein about a scandal involving Irene Adler and a compromising photograph. He deduces details about the invitation note, identifies his visitor as the King of Bohemia, and agrees to try to recover the photograph.

records.l: Dr. Watson, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: Dr. Watson visits Sherlock Holmes at Baker Street and observes Holmes’s deductions and interview with the King. Holmes asks him to remain as a trusted colleague and to return the following afternoon to discuss the case.

records.l: Irene Adler, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: Irene Adler is a former opera singer and adventuress who lives in London. She possesses a photograph of herself with the King of Bohemia and threatens to send it to the family of his intended bride if he marries another woman.

records.l: the King of Bohemia, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein visits Holmes in disguise as Count Von Kramm and reveals that he is the hereditary King of Bohemia. He explains that Irene Adler possesses a compromising photograph and hires Holmes to recover it before the King’s betrothal is publicly proclaimed.

records.l: the House of Ormstein, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: The House of Ormstein is described as the great hereditary royal house of Bohemia. The scandal involving the King and Irene Adler could seriously compromise this reigning family.

records.l: Baker Street, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: Baker Street is the location of Holmes’s rooms, where Dr. Watson visits him and where the King comes to seek help. Holmes remains there surrounded by his books and receives the invitation note at that address.

records.l: kingdom of Bohemia, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: Bohemia is identified as the kingdom ruled by Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein. The paper used for the invitation note was made in Bohemia, and the King’s royal family is involved in the threatened scandal.

records.l: Briony Lodge, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: Briony Lodge, on Serpentine Avenue in St. John’s Wood, is Irene Adler’s address. Holmes records it as the place where he must investigate the photograph.

records.l: the compromising photograph, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: The compromising photograph shows Irene Adler and the King of Bohemia together. The King believes Irene will use it to ruin him by sending it to the family of his intended bride, and he asks Holmes to recover it.

records.l: the compromising letters, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: The King says that he previously wrote Irene Adler compromising letters. Holmes learns that the King wants them back, but the immediate danger concerns the photograph, which Irene also possesses.

records.l: the invitation note, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: The invitation note tells Holmes that a gentleman will visit him at a specified time to discuss a matter of the deepest importance. It warns that the visitor may wear a mask and is written on distinctive paper later linked by Holmes to Bohemia.

records.l: the photograph scandal, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: The photograph scandal concerns Irene Adler’s possession of evidence of her past relationship with the King of Bohemia. If she sends the photograph when the King’s betrothal is publicly proclaimed, it may end his planned marriage and compromise a reigning European family.

records.l: the King's planned marriage, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, I. A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
records.s: The King plans to marry Clotilde Lothman von Saxe-Meningen, the second daughter of the King of Scandinavia. He fears that the photograph scandal will cause her family to end the marriage because of its strict principles and her reputation for delicacy.

records.l: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, II.
records.s: Sherlock Holmes investigates Irene Adler by disguising himself as an unemployed groom and gathering information about her home and associates.
