Holmes believes Moriarty can be defeated, but needs time to act.

records.l: Sherlock Holmes, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Sherlock Holmes is a celebrated, independent amateur detective and crime consultant whose exceptionally active intellect and remarkable powers drive him to investigate difficult cases while helping the police. He is Dr. Watson’s friend and companion, works with Inspector MacDonald and White Mason at Birlstone, and remains loyal to officials when they share a case. He also opposes Professor Moriarty, has visited Moriarty’s rooms three times and once ransacked his papers, yet keeps faith with informant Fred Porlock by refusing to trace him. The account begins when Holmes deciphers Porlock’s cipher using an older edition of Whitaker’s Almanac. The message warns that Douglas is in danger at Birlstone. When John Douglas is reported murdered, Holmes links the warning to possible activity by Moriarty’s organization and travels to investigate. At Birlstone he scrutinizes the study, body, weapon, window, moat, marks, card, footprints, clothing, and especially a missing dumb-bell. He challenges the theory of an outside killer, exposes inconsistencies in Cecil Barker’s account of the candle and lamp, and shows that Barker’s slipper could have made the blood mark on the sill. Holmes concludes that Barker and Mrs. Douglas are concealing facts, though he does not initially decide that they committed murder. By reasoning that the murder occurred earlier than claimed and that the missing dumb-bell was central, Holmes conducts a solitary test: he places a sodden bundle in the moat and uses a proposed draining to provoke its recovery. He identifies Barker as the retriever, finds the dumb-bell, and reveals that Douglas is alive and hidden in the manor; the body could not be Douglas because Douglas’s clothes were recovered from the moat. Holmes urges Douglas to remain alert, warning of danger from American enemies and from English law. In the end, after an enigmatic note and news of Douglas’s death, Holmes judges that Moriarty organized Douglas’s murder from London and says Moriarty can be defeated if given time to plan.

records.l: Dr. Watson, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Dr. Watson is a doctor, detective, and historian of Sherlock Holmes’s group, as well as Holmes’s friend and traveling companion. He receives and discusses Fred Porlock’s cipher message with Holmes, helps consider possible source books, and records the decoded warning. He then accompanies Holmes to Birlstone and the Manor House, where his medical expertise may aid the case. During the investigation, he encounters Mrs. Douglas and Barker, reports to Holmes, discusses murder theories, lends Holmes his umbrella, and shares a room with him. He later helps retrieve a bundle from the moat with the umbrella and receives John Douglas’s written account of the Valley of Fear story.

records.l: Fred Porlock, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Fred Porlock is an assumed name used by a pseudonymous correspondent and subordinate in Professor Moriarty’s criminal organization, described as its only known flawed link. He anonymously warns Sherlock Holmes that danger threatens Douglas, then sends a cipher message from which he withholds the key because Moriarty suspects him and asks Holmes to burn it. Within an hour of the warning, John Douglas is murdered. Holmes does not trace Porlock, keeping his promise of faith.

records.l: Professor Moriarty, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Professor Moriarty is a learned, talented, unmarried professor and the concealed criminal mastermind directing a large London organization. Though publicly unsuspected and earning seven hundred a year, he is very wealthy, owns a Greuze painting, uses accounts at six banks, and may keep wealth abroad. Famous among criminals, he rules with absolute severity, employs and pays Colonel Sebastian Moran six thousand a year, and is feared by members such as Fred Porlock. Holmes describes him as the controlling brain of the underworld. In the death of John Douglas, Moriarty's organization first located Douglas, then advised on the crime; after an agent failed, Moriarty personally intervened.

records.l: Inspector MacDonald, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Inspector MacDonald is a young but trusted Scotland Yard inspector and C.I.D. investigating officer, a London detective from Scotland with a good Aberdeen upbringing. He visits Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson after recognizing Douglas and Birlstone in a decoded message, and reports the murder of Mr. Douglas at Birlstone Manor House. Though he first wants to find Porlock in London, he travels by cab to Birlstone after expecting details from White Mason. At the manor, MacDonald investigates John Douglas's murder closely. He rejects suicide, questions whether an outsider could have escaped after using a noisy shotgun, and recognizes the difficulties in either an inside or outside theory. He questions Cecil Barker and Mrs. Douglas about Douglas's California past, a secret society, marriages, Barker's relationship with Mrs. Douglas, and the missing wedding ring. After Holmes identifies Barker's slipper as the source of a blood mark, MacDonald concludes Barker created the apparent window footprint. Working with White Mason, he traces a suspected outsider and reports a bicycle identification and possible sightings, though these produce arrests in several places. He resists abandoning the case and the plan to drain the moat, but follows Holmes's instructions and sees Barker recover a sodden bundle. Finally, he is astonished that the man investigated was not John Douglas, angrily challenges Holmes over the concealed inquiry, and learns that the earlier search had been misguided.

records.l: John Douglas, The Valley of Fear
records.s: John Douglas is a wealthy, vigorous American-made gentleman of about fifty who lives at Birlstone Manor House in England. Known as fearless, generous, and considerate, he made money in the California gold fields, bears a distinctive branded mark on his forearm, and is shadowed by a long-standing hidden menace from America. Though he is usually fearless, he is nervous about fire, makes nightly rounds of the house, orders the drawbridge raised each night, and believes powerful enemies have pursued him from Chicago and California. He is married to Mrs. Douglas and is jealous of Cecil Barker. At first, Douglas appears to have been horribly murdered at Birlstone: a sawed-off shotgun has inflicted fatal-looking injuries to the face, his wedding ring is missing, and a V.V. 341 card lies nearby. His unease after visiting Tunbridge Wells and the warning sent through Porlock suggest that the danger has finally reached him. The apparent victim, however, is later revealed to be alive and concealed in the Manor House. Ted Baldwin attacked him, but Douglas survived; Baldwin's body was substituted for his own, while Douglas prepared a written account of the Valley of Fear. That account identifies him with Birdy Edwards, Pinkerton's best detective. Under the names Steve Wilson and McMurdo, he infiltrated the Scowrers, gathered evidence, prevented or limited crimes, and helped Captain Marvin arrest the gang. After the Scowrers' convictions, surviving members sought revenge. Edwards changed names, including Douglas and John Douglas, escaped America, amassed a fortune with Barker in California, and settled in England, but remained hunted. Douglas is acquitted for acting in self-defense after the Birlstone affair. Holmes urges him to leave England, yet his flight does not end the pursuit: he travels toward South Africa aboard the Palmyra and is later reported lost overboard near St. Helena.

records.l: Birlstone Manor House, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Birlstone Manor House is an ancient moated Jacobean residence in or near Birlstone, about half a mile from the town. Its estate had been granted to Hugo de Capus by the Red King, and the house stands on the site of an older building. Long, low, and built of dingy liver-coloured brick, it has many gables, diamond-paned windows, a broad water-filled inner moat, and a drawbridge as its only approach; the bridge was raised at night by old custom. After standing empty and decaying, it was occupied by John Douglas and his wife. Its arrangement includes kitchens and pantry at the back, servants' rooms farther behind, and a front study, the fatal room. On January 6 John Douglas was reported murdered in that study, amid clues such as an open window, footprints, blood, a hammer, shotgun, card, and missing wedding ring. Holmes, MacDonald, and White Mason investigate there, while rival explanations concern an intruder and a staged escape. Holmes later watches the house and examines its history and study. The manor's concealed hiding place proves central: Douglas, Barker, and Mrs. Douglas hid Douglas and staged Baldwin's body as his after Baldwin's attack and death, suggesting that a murderer had escaped through the window.
records.t: Birlstone Manor House is an ancient moated Jacobean residence in or near Birlstone, about half a mile from the town. Its estate had been granted to Hugo de Capus by the Red King, and the house stands on the site of an older building. Long, low, and built of dingy liver-coloured brick, it has many gables, diamond-paned windows, a broad water-filled inner moat, and a drawbridge as its only approach; the bridge was raised at night by old custom. After standing empty and decaying, it was occupied by John Douglas and his wife. Its arrangement includes kitchens and pantry at the back, servants' rooms farther behind, and a front study—the fatal room. On January 6 John Douglas was reported murdered in that study, amid clues such as an open window, footprints, blood, a hammer, shotgun, card, and missing wedding ring. Holmes, MacDonald, and White Mason investigate there, while rival explanations concern an intruder and a staged escape. Holmes later watches the house and examines its history and study. The manor's concealed hiding place proves central: Douglas, Barker, and Mrs. Douglas hid Douglas and staged Baldwin's body as his after Baldwin's attack and death, suggesting that a murderer had escaped through the window.

records.l: London, The Valley of Fear
records.s: London is identified by Holmes as the source of the crime against John Douglas, rather than America.

records.l: the cipher message, The Valley of Fear
records.s: A secret book-cipher communication, numerically inscribed through references to words on a page, is decoded by Sherlock Holmes as warning Douglas at Birlstone of imminent danger.

records.l: the anonymous warning letter, The Valley of Fear
records.s: An anonymous communication sent from Camberwell under the name Porlock warns Sherlock Holmes that Mr. Douglas of Birlstone Manor House faces imminent danger. Its coded message is recovered through numbered words in an older Whitaker’s Almanac, and the warning is followed by the death of John Douglas.

records.l: Whitaker’s Almanac, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Whitaker’s Almanac is a standardized common reference book printed in double columns. Holmes first tests its current edition for a cipher without success, then an older edition yields a coded warning of danger to Douglas at Birlstone.

records.l: the book cipher, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The book cipher, found in an anonymous warning letter, encodes messages by page, column, and word numbers; Holmes identifies its common double-column source as an old Whitaker’s Almanac.

records.l: The Tragedy of Birlstone, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Tragedy of Birlstone is a murder at Birlstone Manor House, revealed after Sherlock Holmes decodes a warning concerning Douglas. Douglas is reported horribly murdered in the study, with puzzling evidence: the bell rang violently, no shot was heard by Ames or Mrs. Allen, and Barker claimed the murderer escaped through the study window. MacDonald, Barker, Sergeant Wilson, Dr. Wood, Ames, Mrs. Allen, and the household are drawn into the investigation. The apparent murder is ultimately exposed as a staging: Ted Baldwin died accidentally while attacking Douglas, and Douglas, Barker, and Douglas’s wife made Baldwin’s body appear to be Douglas’s.

records.l: the warning, The Valley of Fear
records.s: concerns the Douglas murder [it anticipates the crime] The warning states that danger may come very soon to Douglas, a rich country gentleman at Birlstone. Its significance is confirmed when Alec MacDonald reports Douglas’s murder.

records.l: the letter from Fred Porlock, The Valley of Fear
records.s: A letter signed by Fred Porlock warns that Professor Moriarty suspects his betrayal, says Porlock will go no further, and asks Sherlock Holmes to burn an unusable cipher message lacking its key.

records.l: the murder of John Douglas, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The murder of John Douglas at Birlstone Manor House is a perplexing, extraordinary apparent homicide and the central crime investigated by the police. Douglas is reported killed shortly before midnight, found with his head almost destroyed by a close-range blast from a sawed-off shotgun. The scene suggests that an attacker hid behind curtains, shot him, and escaped through an open window; it also contains a blood mark, footprints, a missing wedding ring, and a card marked “V.V. 341.” Inspector Alec MacDonald treats the death as murder rather than suicide and later reconstructs Hargrave as the gunman. Holmes challenges the account, arguing that the ring, card, and reported sequence are impossible and that the shot was fired about half an hour before the alarm raised by Barker and Mrs. Douglas. He concludes that a conspiracy concealed the truth. The investigation’s apparent victim is ultimately revealed to be alive, leaving the supposed murder not fully explained.

records.l: White Mason, The Valley of Fear
records.s: White Mason is a quiet, comfortable-looking detective in a loose tweed suit, serving as the local officer at Birlstone and chief Sussex detective. A personal friend of Inspector MacDonald, he recognizes that Mr. Douglas's murder is exceptionally perplexing and asks MacDonald to bring Sherlock Holmes. He briefs Holmes, Dr. Watson, and MacDonald, leads them through the Manor House, examines evidence, and favors an outsider and possible secret-society explanation. He later helps investigate the bicycle and suspect's movements, questions links to Mrs. Douglas, follows Holmes's advice, joins the vigil, and witnesses the recovery of the sodden bundle.

records.l: Birlstone, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Birlstone is a small, ancient Sussex village on the county’s northern border, at the extreme fringe of the Weald forest and ten or twelve miles west of Tunbridge Wells. Picturesque and quiet, it has grown with well-to-do residents and shops. It contains the Manor House, Birlstone house, and the Westville Arms. Jack Douglas rented a secluded house there with Mrs. Douglas, apparently because of danger. After Douglas is murdered, Holmes, Watson, MacDonald, Mason, and the narrator travel to Birlstone to investigate.

records.l: Moriarty's criminal organization, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Moriarty's huge criminal organization unites pickpockets, blackmailers, and card sharpers under death-enforced discipline, using formidable machinery and extravagant resources to locate and destroy John Douglas.

records.l: sawed-off shotgun (Hargrave's shotgun), The Valley of Fear
records.s: Hargrave’s sawed-off shotgun is a weapon and an American shotgun made by the Pennsylvania Small Arms Company, identified from the surviving letters “P-E-N.” Its barrel was cut about a foot before the triggers, leaving it under two feet long and concealable in an overcoat or valise. Loaded with buckshot, its triggers were wired together so that pulling the rear trigger discharged both barrels at once. After being fired at close range, it lay across John Douglas’s chest. The discharge caused Mr. Douglas’s death; MacDonald believes Hargrave deliberately brought and used it in the murder.

records.l: Tunbridge Wells, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Tunbridge Wells is a place in Kent tied to the events before a murder. Mr. Douglas was there before appearing disturbed and saw Ted Baldwin, whom he recognized as a dangerous enemy. Hargrave stayed there two days before the murder, and a bicyclist may have come from it; clothes in the moat were concluded to be his.

records.l: Mrs. Douglas, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Mrs. Douglas is a tall, dark, slender Englishwoman, about thirty and twenty years younger than John Douglas, whom she had married five years earlier after meeting him in a London boarding house. Retiring, devoted to her household, loving, and faithful, she and her husband appeared contented; yet she was uneasy when he returned late and inferred danger from his American past. Though reticent about that past and never having been in America, she believed powerful enemies were tracking him, heard him mention the Valley of Fear and Bodymaster McGinty during a fever, and regarded their wedding as romantic rather than mysterious. After a shot, she came downstairs but was stopped by Cecil Barker, told that Jack was dead, and removed without seeing the body. Trembling and greatly excited, she made no outcry; later she appeared pale and drawn but composed. She told investigators of the enemies and the missing wedding ring. Her laughing privately with Barker and concern about Holmes sharing confidential information raised suspicion. Holmes concluded that she and Barker concealed the truth, conspired to hide the crime, fabricated evidence of an escape through the window, and aided Hargrave's escape. During the later confrontation, she told Barker he had done enough, embraced the man revealed as John Douglas, and urged him to tell his story. She is subsequently described as John Douglas's widow, and Ivy Douglas sent a cable reporting that Jack Douglas was lost overboard near St. Helena in a gale.

records.l: Cecil Barker, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Cecil James Barker is a wealthy English bachelor living at Hales Lodge, Hampstead, and an intimate, loyal friend and California business partner of John Douglas. Tall, sunburned, capable-looking, and masterful, he is a frequent visitor and resident-associated figure at Birlstone Manor House, where his closeness to Mrs. Douglas and Douglas’s jealousy invite suspicion. After a shot is heard at the Manor House, Barker reaches the study within about thirty seconds, reports Douglas’s apparent murder, keeps Mrs. Douglas from entering, and summons the police. He advances the story that an assassin escaped through the open study window and across the moat, citing a blood mark on the sill, and reports a concealed bicycle nearby. He connects Douglas’s danger to his concealed California past and a secret society, while maintaining his loyalty to Douglas and Mrs. Douglas. The apparent escape evidence turns against him: bloodstained carpet slippers belonging to Barker match the mark on the windowsill. Holmes calls Barker’s account a clumsy lie and concludes that he created the false clue to misdirect the investigation. Barker and Mrs. Douglas are understood to be concealing the truth rather than conducting an affair: he assists Douglas in hiding and in staging the scene. He helps dress Ted Baldwin’s body in Douglas’s dressing gown, opens the window, marks the sill, and rings the bell to make it appear that a murderer has fled. He may also have aided Hargrave’s escape. Later, he retrieves a weighted bundle from the moat containing a knife and yellow overcoat, but refuses to explain because the secret is not his to disclose. In the end, Barker brings Holmes the cable reporting Douglas’s death, believes the Scowrers responsible, and reacts with anger and helplessness at the thought of being unable to retaliate against Moriarty.

records.l: Sergeant Wilson, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Sergeant Wilson, a Sussex Constabulary police sergeant, leads a small local station, investigates at the Manor House after midnight, and seeks London assistance when the case exceeds him.

records.l: Dr. Wood, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Dr. Wood, a brisk, capable Birlstone general practitioner, arrives with Sergeant Wilson and Cecil James Barker, confirms John Douglas’s death, and notes his shattered head and forearm brand.

records.l: Ames, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Ames is the prim, respectable, capable butler of Manor House, a faithful servant who had served Sir Charles Chandos for ten years before working for Jack Douglas for five years. During the investigation of Douglas’s murder, he gives a clear, sincere account: he hears the bell, goes with Mrs. Allen to the front of the house, helps enter the room, returns to the study with Barker, and lowers the drawbridge. Shocked and quivering, he identifies the missing wedding ring and Douglas’s branded forearm, describes Douglas as restless and excited, explains the plaster as a shaving cut, and denies seeing the shotgun in the house.

records.l: the drawbridge, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The drawbridge is the wooden bridge over the moat and the only approach to the Manor House. By custom it is raised every evening or night and lowered every morning, though it can be lowered quietly. On the night of the murder it was raised after dusk, from nearly six until Barker lowered it afterward, restricting entry and escape and making the study window seem the only possible escape route; White Mason allows an earlier outsider entry.

records.l: moat, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The inner moat surrounds the Manor House, is about forty feet wide, and is fed by a small stream that continues beyond it. It is normally two feet deep at the sides and three in the middle. An open window and a muddy, blood-like sill mark suggest the murderer waded across, though no clear far-side exit signs are found. Because it is nowhere over three feet deep, Barker says the assassin could not have drowned there.

records.l: the moat, The Valley of Fear
records.s: surrounds Birlstone Manor The moat is where Sherlock Holmes initially finds the weighted bundle and where Cecil Barker later retrieves it. Holmes uses the sound of disturbed water and Barker’s actions to identify who had hidden the bundle.

records.l: lamp (Manor House), The Valley of Fear
records.s: provides a better light [than the candle] The lamp in the study was burning when Ames and Barker returned to the room. Barker said he lit it to obtain better light after seeing what had happened.

records.l: the open window escape, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The open window escape is the inferred flight from the room after Mr. Douglas was shot: a bloody boot-sole smudge on the fully open window sill suggested the murderer went out and waded across the moat. Its timing was hard to explain; MacDonald proposed Hargrave fled, while Holmes suspected Mrs. Douglas and Barker may have helped or arrived first.

records.l: blood mark (Manor House window sill), The Valley of Fear
records.s: A blood smudge on a Manor House window sill, examined by Holmes, is identified as a remarkably broad, possibly splay-footed shoe tread unlike other indistinct footprints.

records.l: card marked V.V. 341, The Valley of Fear
records.s: A rough cardboard card, rudely inscribed in thick ink “V.V. 341,” is found beside John Douglas’s body. Wilson cannot interpret it; Barker says he had not seen it and believes the murderer left it. Holmes links it, with a branded mark, to a possible secret society.

records.l: the hammer, The Valley of Fear
records.s: A workmanlike hammer found by the fireplace is examined without signs of violence or blood; a possible struggle is suggested, but its use remains unestablished.

records.l: the brand on John Douglas's forearm, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The object is a brown branded mark: a triangle inside a circle on John Douglas’s right forearm. It is a burn, not a tattoo, and it must have caused considerable pain. Barker and Ames had seen it many times. Holmes considers it potentially connected with the card marked V.V. 341. The same lodge mark appears on Baldwin’s forearm, leading Douglas to use the resemblance to make Baldwin’s body seem to be his own.

records.l: the wedding ring, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The wedding ring is John or Mr. Douglas’s plain gold ring, worn on the little finger of his left hand beneath a nugget ring. After Douglas’s death, it is missing: an unknown person removed it, while the nugget ring was removed and replaced, suggesting deliberate taking. White Mason supposes the killer demanded it before shooting Douglas, but its purpose is unknown. MacDonald finds the removal extraordinary and considers whether it connects Douglas’s marriage to the tragedy, though Barker rejects any reflection on Mrs. Douglas’s honour. Holmes doubts the reported removal-and-replacement account and considers that an avenger may have taken it in connection with Douglas’s first marriage.

records.l: the mystery, The Valley of Fear
records.s: concerns the murder of John Douglas [the strange events at Birlstone Manor House] The mystery involves how a murderer entered the Manor House despite the raised drawbridge, killed John Douglas, and escaped through the open window. The hidden figure, the V.V. 341 card, the branded forearm, and the missing wedding ring leave the circumstances unexplained.

records.l: America, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_a place [where Mr. Douglas had lived before England] America is identified as the place where Mr. Douglas had lived before his marriage. Mrs. Douglas believes that events there left him in danger from powerful enemies.

records.l: England, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_a country [destination of Edwards’s escape] England is presented as unsafe for John Douglas after his acquittal. Holmes warns that forces in England may be more dangerous than those Douglas had escaped.

records.l: the Eminent Order of Freemen, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Eminent Order of Freemen is a society organized through lodges, with a stated identity as a benefit club for charity and good fellowship. McMurdo, a member of Lodge No. 29 in Chicago, says its lodges throughout the country provide members with friends; membership is proved by a hand-grip, gesture, sign, and countersign, and Freemen settling in Vermissa must join the local lodge. In Vermissa, however, the Order is identified with the Scowrers. Its apparent social and charitable purpose gives way to a coercive secret criminal society: its bosses control members by threats, punishment, and violence, and opposition brings retaliation. Its members commit murder, intimidation, blackmail, mutilation, attacks, and explosions, terrorizing mine owners, other opponents, and the district as a whole. Killings at Crow Hill and Stake Royal deepen the shadow over Vermissa, while the local lodge is associated with the attack on the Herald office. McMurdo becomes an increasingly important adviser, even as citizens begin organizing and distributing firearms against the terror. In the later investigation of Jack Douglas’s death, Holmes, White Mason, and Inspector MacDonald treat the existence of such a secret society as a working hypothesis, and Barker believes it relentlessly pursued Douglas until his killing.

records.l: the police, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The police investigate Jack Douglas’s murder, examine weapons and the area, and seek a wet stranger who may have crossed the moat. Alerted by Barker, they find no suspect but locate a bicycle near the Manor House.

records.l: suicide of Mr. Douglas, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_ruled_out_by investigation [the investigators regard suicide as impossible] White Mason and Inspector MacDonald reject the possibility of suicide. They conclude that suicide cannot account for the concealed wedding ring, the staged footprints, the opened window, the blood on the sill, and the other signs.

records.l: the John Douglas case, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The John Douglas case concerns Douglas's murder and an investigation at the Manor House. Investigators consider whether the killer was an insider or outsider, examine physical clues, statements, timing, a blood mark, wedding ring, bicycle, and missing dumb-bell, while Holmes tests how sound travels through the house. Holmes says their approach is hopeless because they misunderstand the case, but pursues a shorter path to the truth. Referred to a higher court, Douglas is acquitted for self-defense; his later reported death suggests a planned murder organized from London.

records.l: window (Manor House), The Valley of Fear
records.s: The window immediately right of the drawbridge is open after the murder. Though narrow, it can admit a person; its bloodstain and the raised drawbridge lead investigators, including Barker, to regard it as the suspected murderer’s escape route.

records.l: the candle, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is a poor light source [according to Cecil Barker] The candle in the study was lit when Barker entered after the crime. Barker said he blew it out because it gave poor light and then lit the lamp.

records.l: the missing dumb-bell, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The missing dumb-bell, one of a pair, becomes central after its mate is found under a side table and no one knows whether there was another. Sherlock Holmes says the case hangs on it. Its absence suggests something sunk in nearby water; it is found in the moat attached to a sodden bundle, used to weight it, and removed.

records.l: the bicycle, The Valley of Fear
records.s: A well-used Rudge-Whitworth bicycle, splashed from a considerable journey, is found concealed near the Manor House with a saddlebag holding a spanner and oilcan. Left as a supposed means of escape, it is investigated for its likely owner. Holmes doubts that a fugitive would abandon such a means of escape. The Eagle Commercial’s manager identifies it as Hargrave’s; MacDonald concludes Hargrave concealed and abandoned it because it could identify him.

records.l: footprints (Manor House), The Valley of Fear
records.s: are_indistinct very indistinct [in the mud-stained corner] Indistinct footprints appear in the mud-stained corner behind the curtain and are treated as evidence that someone waited there. The tread on the window sill appears remarkably broad and splay-footed, while the traceable sole in the corner seems more shapely.

records.l: California, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_a place [location of Edwards’s later refuge and work] Jack Douglas lived and worked in California for about five years with Cecil Barker, becoming partners in a successful mining claim at Benito Canyon. Douglas suddenly left for England, and within a week several hard-looking American men came asking where he was.

records.l: Chicago, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Chicago is a city tied to McMurdo’s past: he came from Lodge 29 there, fled after trouble connected with Jonas Pinto’s shooting and counterfeit money, though no clear case was made against him. It is also where Edwards became a Freemen, later married Ettie, survived two attempts on his life, and departed under a changed name for California.

records.l: Douglas's death, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Douglas's death occurred in the study while he was wearing a dressing gown and had left his revolver in the bedroom. Barker said Douglas might have believed he was safe once the drawbridge was raised.

records.l: Douglas's marriage to Mrs. Douglas, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Douglas's marriage to Mrs. Douglas was questioned because his wedding ring was missing and because Barker acknowledged that Douglas had been jealous of his friendship with his wife. Barker insisted that Mrs. Douglas was loving and faithful.

records.l: the danger from Mr. Douglas's American past, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The danger from Mr. Douglas's American past, associated by him with the Valley of Fear, was a long-persisting feud. Beginning at least eleven years earlier, it shadowed his life through threatening men in California and powerful enemies he believed were pursuing him. He concealed it from Mrs. Douglas, though his precautions, fear of strangers, and references revealed it.

records.l: Ettie Shafter, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Ettie Shafter is Jacob Shafter’s nineteen-year-old, blonde, fair-haired daughter, a young woman of singular beauty who runs the Shafter boarding house after her mother’s death. Her life is darkened by fear of the Scowrers and of Teddy Baldwin, to whom she is bound only by a half-promise that she rejects. Although Baldwin and McMurdo contend over her, she is recognized as free to choose. Ettie loves Jack McMurdo deeply and becomes secretly, increasingly intimate with him, while fearing that his apparent criminal life and association with the lodge will destroy them. She repeatedly urges McMurdo to flee with her and her father, proposing other cities, the West, or Europe; he initially refuses, then promises eventual departure. When he later signals, she agrees to the escape, receives a sealed note from Scanlan, and leaves the Valley of Fear by special train with her muffled lover. Ten days later she marries Edwards in Chicago, witnessed by Jacob Shafter. Later she is identified as John Douglas’s wife: she initially knows little of his past, helps Douglas and Barker conceal his survival after Baldwin’s death, learns the full story, and is someone Douglas hopes to rejoin after escaping.

records.l: the bell, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The bell rang violently after Douglas was killed, bringing Ames, Mrs. Allen, and eventually the others to the front of the house. Its ringing was heard even though the shot itself was not heard by the servants.

records.l: the study, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The study is the murder scene where Barker finds Mr. Douglas dead on the floor after an apparent gunshot. It contains a candle and lamp, the missing dumb-bell before it is put in the moat, and later a sodden bundle beneath the writing table. Its changing light, view over the moat, and preserved scene draw Holmes to spend an evening there seeking clues.

records.l: the bloodstain, The Valley of Fear
records.s: supports the assassin [as evidence of escape through the window] The bloodstain was considered by Barker to be conclusive evidence that the murderer escaped through the study window.

records.l: the gunshot, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The gunshot, apparently causing Mr. Douglas’s murder, was probably fired at a quarter to eleven. Mrs. Allen heard what seemed to be a slamming door, while Mrs. Douglas heard the shooting, came downstairs in her dressing gown, and was stopped by Cecil Barker, who said she could do nothing.

records.l: Hargrave, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Hargrave is an American traveler and suspected assassin who stays at the Eagle Commercial in Tunbridge Wells under his own name, with no papers, letters, or address recorded. About five foot nine, around fifty, grizzled and gray-moustached, he is fierce-looking and wears several heavy garments. He travels by bicycle and carries a valise concealing a sawed-off shotgun. After leaving the hotel he disappears; Barker believes he escaped through a study window, leaving his bicycle behind. Later cyclist reports conflict, and Holmes dismisses tracing him as unhelpful.

records.l: Douglas's jealousy, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is a fault of Jack Douglas Douglas's jealousy concerned his friendship with Cecil Barker and Mrs. Douglas. Barker said Douglas could become angry when he saw sympathy between them, despite loving both his wife and his friend.

records.l: the alleged affair between Barker and Mrs. Douglas, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_denied by Cecil Barker [implicitly and indignantly] The alleged affair between Barker and Mrs. Douglas was raised by Inspector MacDonald's questions about whether Douglas approved of their friendship. Barker refused to answer at first, then denied any implication against Mrs. Douglas's honour and declared that she was faithful.

records.l: Boss McGinty, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Boss McGinty, also called Jack or Black Jack McGinty and later John McGinty, is the feared Bodymaster and dominant boss of Vermissa Lodge 341 and the Scowrers. A tall, powerful, black-haired saloon-keeper with a rough, jovial manner, he owns or runs the Union House, where the lodge meets, while also holding public offices as municipal councillor and commissioner of roads. Popular with rough townspeople but feared throughout the township, he is believed to wield pitiless secret powers and is associated with neglected works, falsified accounts, and public blackmail. Nothing in the district is thought able to happen against his will. McGinty tests the newcomer McMurdo at gunpoint, accepts his criminal experience and counterfeit dollars, stops Baldwin's quarrel with him, and requires him to attend the lodge. He conducts McMurdo's initiation, presides over violent assignments, boasts that the lodge can command two hundred men and evade police and courts, and uses threats against dissenters such as Brother Morris. He orders a severe warning for James Stanger rather than his death, supplies McMurdo an alibi and promises legal help, and increasingly treats McMurdo as a valuable instrument. After celebrating killings at Crow Hill and Gilmerton, he assigns McMurdo to murder Chester Wilcox. Though he dismisses reports of danger, McGinty accepts McMurdo's warning about Birdy Edwards and helps arrange the supposed detective's capture at Widow MacNamara's house. The plan fails: Captain Marvin traps and arrests McGinty and the other Scowrers. After trial, McGinty is hanged with his followers. Earlier, while feverish, Mr. Douglas repeatedly speaks McGinty's name with anger and horror, and Mrs. Douglas connects him with the Valley of Fear.

records.l: the garden, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The garden beside the village inn, flanked by strange-cut ancient yews, contains a central old sundial, lawn, and concealed stone seat; behind its hedge, Mrs. Douglas and Barker talk and laugh after Mr. Douglas’s death.

records.l: the Valley of Fear, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Valley of Fear is Mr. Douglas’s name for a dangerous part of his American past, identified by Sherlock Holmes with Vermissa Valley, a coal and iron valley in the United States. It was long controlled and haunted by the violent Scowrers, leaving its people without hope despite the coming of spring; its terror was especially dark in early summer 1875. Edwards exposes the organization, leading to arrests and prosecutions and freeing the valley from its control, but surviving Scowrers later pursue him for revenge.

records.l: Mr. Barker's carpet slippers, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Mr. Barker's carpet slippers, found under the hall chair with bloodstained soles, include one that exactly matches a blood mark on the study window sill, suggesting Barker made it.

records.l: the enemies from America, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Enemies from America are believed to be powerful and connected with Mr. Douglas’s American life. They pursued him from Chicago to California, drove him out of America, and kept him constantly on guard. He hoped Baldwin’s apparent success in killing him would end their hunt, but they may still threaten him.

records.l: the police, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The police defend the Herald office with armed guards after an attack, arrest McMurdo and others, but their case fails because witnesses cannot identify attackers and the bench criticizes excessive zeal.

records.l: the village inn, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The village inn is Dr. Watson’s modest lodging and Holmes’s tea stop, where Holmes returns around five, eats substantially, and discusses the case with Watson.

records.l: the conspiracy, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Holmes believes Barker and Mrs. Douglas are involved in a conspiracy to conceal the truth about the murder. He also considers an alternative in which they are not the murderers but were threatened by an outsider and then delayed the alarm to protect themselves from suspicion.

records.l: valise (Hargrave's valise), The Valley of Fear
records.s: Hargrave's small, unmarked London-made valise holds British contents and a sawed-off shotgun; after MacDonald and Mason return at nightfall, MacDonald believes it could have concealed the gun.

records.l: single dumb-bell (Mr. Douglas's dumb-bell), The Valley of Fear
records.s: Sherlock Holmes repeatedly returns to the question of why an athletic man would develop his frame using the unnatural instrument of a single dumb-bell. He makes a private investigation of this matter during the night.

records.l: investigation into Mr. Douglas's murder, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The investigation advances when MacDonald and White Mason identify Hargrave's bicycle and obtain a description of him. Holmes remains dissatisfied with their explanation and pursues a separate line of inquiry involving the timing of the murder, the suspected concealment, and the single dumb-bell.

records.l: conspiracy to conceal the crime, The Valley of Fear
records.s: At nightfall, Holmes tells MacDonald and White Mason that Mrs. Douglas and Barker conspired to conceal what happened, aiding or preceding the murderer's escape.

records.l: fabricated evidence of escape, The Valley of Fear
records.s: concerns Hargrave's escape [through the window] Sherlock Holmes believes that Mrs. Douglas and Barker fabricated evidence suggesting that the murderer escaped through the window. He considers this part of their effort to conceal the crime.

records.l: Vermissa, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Vermissa is a town in the United States, the central township at the head of Vermissa Valley and the largest town on the railroad line. A bleak, dirty mining settlement of wooden houses, stores, saloons, gaming houses, mines, and factories, it includes the Union House, McGinty’s saloon, Widow MacNamara’s lodging house, and Lodge 341. The lodge operates from the Union House and, with the Scowrers and the Freeman’s society, dominates the coal district through violence, extortion, murder, and retaliation. Small owners are driven out, police cannot secure convictions, and residents fear both the organization and possible intervention by authorities. By the end, citizens begin to unite against the terror amid rumors of secret meetings and firearms.

records.l: Vermissa Valley, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Vermissa Valley is a desolate coal and iron valley in the United States, containing the Vermissa coal and iron district, mining and iron-working settlements, furnaces, slag heaps, smoke, and crowded worker housing. Its defining reality is the Scowrers’ criminal control: their lodges, including Lodge 341, enforce fear and violence across Vermissa and the surrounding thirty-mile valley. Residents are said to know criminals’ identities but fear testifying, while murder threatens the population from dusk until dawn. Boss McGinty is feared throughout the region, and the lodge’s power is used against mine owners and others who resist it. As McMurdo travels through this grim, snowy setting, joins its orbit, and faces growing danger, Birdy Edwards investigates the Scowrers, while McMurdo expects the violence may force him and Ettie to leave.

records.l: the sodden bundle, The Valley of Fear
records.s: A sodden bundle retrieved from the moat is weighted with a dumb-bell and hidden beneath the study writing table, containing boots, clothing, and a sheathed deadly knife.

records.l: the yellow overcoat, The Valley of Fear
records.s: conceals the concealed fowling piece [inside its prolonged inner pocket] The yellow overcoat in the sodden bundle has an inner pocket extended into the lining to hold a truncated fowling piece. Its tailor’s label reads “Neal, Outfitter, Vermissa, U.S.A.”

records.l: the moat-draining plan, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is a ruse [intended to make the bundle's concealer retrieve it] The moat-draining plan is announced to make the person who hid the bundle remove it before the water is diverted. The plan succeeds when Cecil Barker retrieves the bundle at night, giving Holmes and the others witnesses to his action.

records.l: the Valley of Fear story, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Valley of Fear story is John Douglas’s written account, prepared during confinement and given to Dr. Watson. It recounts Douglas’s pursuit by enemies from America, Ted Baldwin’s attack, Baldwin’s accidental death, and Douglas’s plan to conceal himself by presenting Baldwin as the victim, while insisting he has told the truth.

records.l: Ted Baldwin, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Ted Baldwin is a violent Scowrer and higher official of Lodge 341, marked on the forearm with the lodge’s branded circle-and-triangle symbol. A boss and enforcer in Vermissa, he claims Ettie Shafter as his woman and becomes McMurdo’s enemy over her. Though he challenges McGinty’s favor toward McMurdo, McGinty forces him to reconcile publicly; Baldwin remains resentful as McMurdo rises. He eagerly leads the assault on James Stanger, beating him until McMurdo stops him, and later leads the party that murders William Hales, for which the lodge honors him. Baldwin is identified by John Douglas as the worst among his pursuers. He secretly enters Birlstone Manor to attack Douglas with a knife and buckshot gun, but during their struggle the gun fires into Baldwin’s face and kills him. His body is then disguised as Douglas’s.

records.l: English law, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_a just law [in the main] Douglas asks how he stands under English law after concealing his survival and substituting Baldwin's body for his own. Holmes says that English law is generally just and that Douglas will receive no worse than his deserts.

records.l: the dead bicyclist from Tunbridge Wells, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Holmes identifies the body found at Birlstone Manor as belonging not to Douglas but to the bicyclist from Tunbridge Wells, based on the suit of clothes discovered in the moat. Douglas's account identifies the dead man more specifically as Ted Baldwin.

records.l: Ted Baldwin's attack on John Douglas, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Baldwin entered the study at Birlstone Manor and sprang at Douglas with a knife. Douglas struck at him with a hammer, seized Baldwin's gun, and struggled with him until the weapon discharged both barrels into Baldwin's face.

records.l: the hiding place at Birlstone Manor, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_known_by Ames [before the events] Douglas used a known hiding place at Birlstone Manor after Baldwin's death. Holmes had suspected that Douglas was concealed somewhere in the house because it offered suitable shelter for a fugitive.

records.l: the buckshot gun, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_possessed_by Ted Baldwin [used in his attack on John Douglas] Baldwin carried a buckshot gun, which Douglas believed could have killed him if Baldwin had confronted him outside. During their struggle inside the study, the gun discharged and killed Baldwin.

records.l: the suit of clothes, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_used_to_disguise Ted Baldwin [as John Douglas’s corpse] Douglas brought down his suit of clothes and put Baldwin's body in Douglas's dressing gown while sending Baldwin's own clothes through the window in a weighted bundle. Holmes found the suit in the moat and used it to determine that the body was not Douglas's.

records.l: the mystery of the past, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_solved_by John Douglas's story [after the earlier events are narrated] The narrative postpones the origins of Douglas's conflict and moves back approximately twenty years and thousands of miles westward to recount them. The earlier events are presented as necessary to resolve the mystery of the past before the story returns to Baker Street.

records.l: McMurdo, The Valley of Fear
records.s: McMurdo is a young Irishman, a well-educated, sociable, quick-witted traveler from Chicago who arrives in Vermissa as a self-confessed fugitive from justice. Fresh-complexioned and middle-sized, with brown hair, large gray eyes, spectacles, and a loaded navy revolver, he is charming and communicative but prone to fierce anger and bitterly contemptuous of police. He is also a counterfeiter and murderer: in Chicago he made false dollars and killed Jonas Pinto after Pinto threatened to expose their work. At Jacob Shafter’s boarding house, McMurdo becomes conspicuous through his wit, singing, education, and fearlessness. He loves Ettie Shafter and clashes with Ted Baldwin over her. His prior membership in Lodge 29 of the Eminent Order of Freemen brings him to Boss McGinty and Lodge 341 in Vermissa. He proves himself dangerous by admitting his crimes, holding McGinty at pistol point during a test, enduring branding and initiation, swearing secrecy and fidelity, and accepting McGinty’s authority. McMurdo rapidly gains influence among the lodge. He approves its violence, assists in the attack on James Stanger while preventing Baldwin from killing him, survives arrest and acquittal, and earns a reputation for fighting and for planning violent work. Though Ettie asks him to leave, he refuses, promising to find an honourable way out within a year. He accepts an assignment against Chester Wilcox, leads Manders and Reilly in an unsuccessful killing attempt, and continues pursuing Wilcox after an ensuing shooting. By the end, McMurdo is Inner Deacon, necessary to lodge councils, and considered a possible successor to McGinty. As danger from the Pinkerton investigation rises, he destroys incriminating papers, warns the lodge, recognizes Birdy Edwards under another name, and helps plan an ambush. At the same time, he and Ettie prepare to escape the valley together.

records.l: Scanlan, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Scanlan is a small, sharp-faced, nervous black-eyed man, a Lodge 341 Scowrer and fellow member of the Eminent Order of Freemen who lives in Hobson’s Patch. Though secretly horrified by lodge violence, he urges McMurdo to report at once to Boss McGinty. McMurdo’s original train acquaintance, Scanlan moves in at Widow MacNamara’s, lodges with him, leads him home drunk, and is told to put liquor on the lodge table.

records.l: Jacob Shafter, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Jacob Shafter is an honest boarding-house keeper on Sheridan Street in Vermissa and Ettie Shafter’s father. He takes McMurdo as a paying boarder, warns him that the Freemen are the Scowrers, and orders him out, fearing danger amid Baldwin’s courtship of Ettie. Later he saves money, feeds McMurdo, and witnesses Ettie’s marriage to Birdy Edwards in Chicago.

records.l: the miners, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The miners at Crow Hill witness attacks, initially helpless; some advance, gunfire scatters them, and a brave few return to the mine.

records.l: the Scowrers, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Scowrers are a secret, organized criminal gang, also called the violent local members of the Eminent Order of Freemen, operating through lodges in the coal district and dominating Vermissa and the Valley of Fear. Said to have at least five hundred members, they are led by older members who order younger agents to act. They maintain power through terror, violence, loyal supporters, intimidation of witnesses, alibis, and money for legal defense, escaping convictions during ten years of outrage. Their repeated crimes include murder, shootings, beatings, mutilation, violent intimidation, an attack on the Herald office, and the blowing up of a family; their rule leaves the community afraid to speak openly. Opposition eventually gathers among citizens, corporations, railroads, and the Pinkerton organization. When the lodge plans to capture and kill Birdy Edwards as an informant, he reveals himself as a Pinkerton detective. The gang is surrounded, disarmed, arrested, tried, punished, and broken up, though sixty more members remain beyond those captured. In the epilogue, they are still considered capable of murdering John Douglas, but Holmes says they did not act alone.
records.t: The Scowrers are a secret, organized criminal gang—also called the violent local members of the Eminent Order of Freemen—operating through lodges in the coal district and dominating Vermissa and the Valley of Fear. Said to have at least five hundred members, they are led by older members who order younger agents to act. They maintain power through terror, violence, loyal supporters, intimidation of witnesses, alibis, and money for legal defense, escaping convictions during ten years of outrage. Their repeated crimes include murder, shootings, beatings, mutilation, violent intimidation, an attack on the Herald office, and the blowing up of a family; their rule leaves the community afraid to speak openly. Opposition eventually gathers among citizens, corporations, railroads, and the Pinkerton organization. When the lodge plans to capture and kill Birdy Edwards as an informant, he reveals himself as a Pinkerton detective. The gang is surrounded, disarmed, arrested, tried, punished, and broken up, though sixty more members remain beyond those captured. In the epilogue, they are still considered capable of murdering John Douglas, but Holmes says they did not act alone.

records.l: Lodge 341, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Lodge 341 is a lodge of the Ancient Order of Freemen in Vermissa Valley and the organized body of the Scowrers. Led by Bodymaster Boss McGinty, it has about sixty members, meets on Saturday nights in a reserved room at the Union House, and is guarded by ranks, coded signs, and secret tests. Its local initiation requires courage, endurance of pain, secrecy, fidelity, and branding, while McGinty enforces discipline heavily. McMurdo is ordered to attend and become affiliated. Later, the lodge hears his warning about Birdy Edwards, appoints a committee, and approves an ambush plan.

records.l: Vermissa Lodge, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Vermissa Lodge is a lodge of the Eminent Order of Freemen and a criminal association in the coal and iron district, under Jack McGinty’s authority, with Ted Baldwin among its members. It exchanges violent services with other lodges, extorts local firms, supports families of members killed on lodge work, and pursues a murder campaign through discussed assassinations, arson, intimidation, and attacks against those judged by its lodges.

records.l: the evening train, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The evening train runs on a single-track railroad, connecting coal-mining and iron-working settlements as it carries workers and travelers from Stagville toward Vermissa amid conversations, quarrels, and recognition.

records.l: Shafter's boarding house, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Shafter's boarding house stands back from Sheridan Street in Vermissa, run by Jacob Shafter with Ettie. It temporarily houses ten or a dozen boarders and becomes McMurdo's lodging when he pays in advance, but Shafter soon orders him to leave after one more night, fearing a Freeman.

records.l: Hobson’s Patch, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_a place [location of the detective’s mission and police presence] Hobson’s Patch is where Birdy Edwards, under the name Steve Wilson, is lodging. McMurdo plans to go there to locate him through the telegraph operator.

records.l: Sheridan Street, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Sheridan Street in Vermissa is the location of Jacob Shafter’s boarding house. McMurdo gives it as the address where he can be found.

records.l: the Union House, The Valley of Fear
records.s: contains Lodge 341, Vermissa [its reserved assembly room] The Union House is a saloon that nearly has the dignity of a hotel and is run by Jack McGinty. Brother Scanlan advises McMurdo to go there and see McGinty if he gets into trouble.

records.l: the Scowrers’ affairs, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Scowrers’ affairs are the notorious matters most often discussed in Vermissa, and they are associated with killings and intimidation. A miner refuses to speak openly about them and warns McMurdo that even mentioning McGinty in connection with them is dangerous.

records.l: McMurdo’s flight from justice, The Valley of Fear
records.s: leads_to McMurdo’s arrival in Vermissa [through his move from Chicago] McMurdo’s flight from justice began in Chicago, where he says he had plenty of work but left because of trouble. He hints that the trouble may have involved imprisonment and possibly killing, but he refuses to explain further.

records.l: McMurdo’s arrival in Vermissa, The Valley of Fear
records.s: occurs_on 1875-02-04 McMurdo arrives in Vermissa by train carrying a leather gripsack and a loaded revolver. He is escorted toward the Shafter house by a miner, meets Ettie and Jacob Shafter, and settles there as a boarder.

records.l: the murders attributed to the Scowrers, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The murders attributed to the Scowrers include Milman, Van Shorst, the Nicholson family, Mr. Hyam, and Billy James. Presented as common knowledge, they reveal a murder society that silences witnesses and protects accused men with false alibis.

records.l: McMurdo's membership in the Freemen, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_a membership in the Eminent Order of Freemen McMurdo says that he has been a member of the lodge for over two years and initially understands it as an innocent society found throughout the United States. He later tells Ettie that he is a Freeman himself and suggests that he may be no better than the other members.

records.l: McMurdo's proposed confrontation with McGinty, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_intended_to secure McGinty's favor [by reporting immediately to him] After Baldwin threatens him and Ettie urges him to seek protection, McMurdo decides to go immediately to Boss McGinty and make matters right. He intends to get his word in first and secure McGinty's friendship before the Scowrers move against him.

records.l: McGinty's saloon, The Valley of Fear
records.s: McGinty’s saloon, in Market Square, is a crowded favourite gathering place for the town’s rougher elements, where McMurdo meets McGinty, is questioned behind the bar, and witnesses McGinty confront Ted Baldwin.

records.l: counterfeit dollars, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Counterfeit dollars made by McMurdo in Chicago enter circulation; they resemble genuine dollars so closely that McGinty cannot distinguish them and sees their value to the lodge.

records.l: the quarrel between McMurdo and Baldwin, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The quarrel between McMurdo and Baldwin concerns a young lady whom both men appear to claim. McMurdo offers to fight Baldwin, but McGinty rules that the lady is free to choose and forces the men to perform the lodge's reconciliation ceremony. McMurdo declares that he bears no grudge, while Baldwin complies reluctantly and remains sullen.

records.l: the lodge meeting, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The lodge meeting covers violent assignments, financial affairs, extortion payments, and the organization's response to criticism. McGinty presides over the proceedings, while Brother Morris's warnings about the lodge's growing danger are met with hostility and intimidation.

records.l: Captain Marvin, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Captain Marvin, formerly an ordinary civil police officer in Chicago, is captain of the Mine Police. He identifies Jack McMurdo through the Chicago shooting of Jonas Pinto, then leads police to McMurdo’s house, disarms and arrests him over the Herald office attack and searches unsuccessfully for a coining plant. Later, assisting Birdy Edwards, he surrounds Edwards’s house, stops McGinty, disarms the Scowrers, and takes them into custody.

records.l: the branding, The Valley of Fear
records.s: marks Jack McMurdo [with a circle and triangle on the right forearm] The branding is a painful lodge mark placed on McMurdo’s right forearm during his initiation. It consists of a circle with a triangle inside it, left deep and red by a branding iron; other lodge members show that they bear the same mark.

records.l: the Scowrers' terror and criminal rule, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Scowrers’ terror and criminal rule is their oppressive control of Vermissa and the Valley of Fear through fear, organized assaults, and murder. Over ten years, they attack even people who have not harmed or been seen by them, face no convictions, and boast about fatal violence. Their rule also coerces members into killing and makes departure dangerous, threatening families. By early summer 1875 their dominance is at its height: they are armed, powerful, and confident. It begins to weaken when organized law and investigation make their leaders fear retribution.

records.l: the oath of secrecy and fidelity, The Valley of Fear
records.s: An oath binds Jack McMurdo to secrecy about lodge business, threatening instant inevitable death for breach; he later tells Ettie Shafter it forbids disclosure, abandonment of comrades, or leaving with secrets.

records.l: Brother Morris, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Brother Morris is a drygoods-store owner on Market Square, husband and father of three, and a reluctant, troubled member of Vermissa lodge and the Freeman’s society. Coerced into crime, including his employer’s murder, he fears for his wife and children and is excommunicated because he is a Scowrer. He opposes Boss McGinty and the lodge’s criminal rule, warning that attacks such as the proposed killing of James Stanger will bring police, troops, courts, and the lodge’s destruction. Threatened by McGinty, he recants publicly, but privately trusts McMurdo, offers him a clerkship, and describes Vermissa as ruled by fear. Finally, Morris gives McMurdo a telegraph-service friend’s letter warning of a Pinkerton detective and asks him to handle the danger.

records.l: Chester Wilcox, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Chester Wilcox is a scarred former colour sergeant and chief foreman of the Iron Dike Company, known for being armed and a quick, accurate shot. Targeted by the Scowrers and the Society of Freemen after shooting Jim Carnaway, he survives two earlier attempts on his life. Ordered attacked by Jack McMurdo at his isolated home, he moves his family to safer, less-known quarters under police protection, where he is later reportedly fired upon from ambush.

records.l: Editor Stanger, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Editor Stanger, an elderly and respected Vermissa newspaper editor of the Herald and Daily Herald, writes “Law and Order!” against lodge violence. McGinty orders a severe warning, and Baldwin with other members beats Stanger in his office, though McMurdo stops Baldwin from killing him. Stanger survives without immediate danger of death and later testifies that he can identify only a moustached first attacker.

records.l: Vermissa Herald, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Vermissa Herald is a newspaper published in Vermissa. After it publishes “Law and Order!” criticizing the lodge’s violence, lodge members assault its worker James Stanger at the office while the press operates.

records.l: the initiation ceremony, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The lodge initiation leaves McMurdo with a painful branded arm and the effects of heavy drinking. It binds him to the lodge through an oath of loyalty and introduces him to its violent discipline.

records.l: the attack on the Herald office, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The attack on the Herald office is a lodge-ordered warning against James Stanger for criticizing the lodge. At McGinty's direction, Ted Baldwin organizes several members to beat Stanger in the Vermissa Herald office. McMurdo prevents Baldwin from killing him, and the attackers escape using an alibi at the Union Bar. Stanger suffers severe head injuries; arrests follow, but uncertain witnesses prevent identification.

records.l: the murder campaign, The Valley of Fear
records.s: targets local people [including men with no personal connection to the lodge] The murder campaign is described as a long-running series of assassinations and other violent acts carried out by the criminal organization. The lodge treats violence as reciprocal service between lodges and provides financial support to the families of members killed during its operations.

records.l: the lodge's extortion, The Valley of Fear
records.s: targets local firms [demanding payment for protection or noninterference] The lodge extorts money from local companies in exchange for leaving them alone. Max Linder & Co. pays five hundred dollars, Walker Brothers is pressed for five dollars after offering one hundred, and other companies make regular contributions; the lodge has also used arson and threats to force compliance.

records.l: the article “Law and Order!”, The Valley of Fear
records.s: “Law and Order!”, written by James Stanger, condemns Vermissa’s murders, criminal organization, and terror; after McGinty reads it at a meeting and dismisses it as “slush,” he orders a violent warning against Stanger.

records.l: Miller Hill, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Miller Hill is a winter-deserted public park in Vermissa, overlooking town, valley, mines, factories, and ranges; Brother Morris meets McMurdo there privately.

records.l: the Herald office, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Herald office is attacked by Scowrers opposing editorials, hosts citizens’ secret gatherings, then is attacked by Freeman’s society and defended by police guards.

records.l: the arrest and acquittal of Jack McMurdo, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Jack McMurdo is arrested at home by Captain Marvin while Boss McGinty visits, then spends a night in a common cell with Baldwin and other accused men, aided by lodge members’ whisky and cards. At the next day’s hearing he is discharged, and his acquittal increases his popularity and reputation for boldness among the Scowrers.

records.l: the court hearing, The Valley of Fear
records.s: discharges McMurdo [for insufficient evidence] At the court hearing, witnesses for the prosecution admit that they cannot confidently identify the attackers, while six citizens testify that the accused men were at a card party during the attack. The magistrate dismisses the case and nearly apologizes to the defendants, while implicitly censuring Captain Marvin and the police.

records.l: Lawler, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Lawler, an experienced, abstinent assassin with fourteen society commissions, arrives in Vermissa with Andrews under County Delegate orders for a secret operation whose target he withholds.

records.l: Andrews, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Andrews, a young, cheerful abstaining assassin, completes three killings for the society and shoots Josiah H. Dunn during the Crow Hill attack.

records.l: Crow Hill, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Crow Hill, a large mine managed by Josiah H. Dunn, maintains order amid terror until Lawler, Andrews, and accomplices attack and murder Dunn and engineer Menzies.

records.l: Iron Dike Company, The Valley of Fear
records.s: employs Chester Wilcox [as chief foreman] The Iron Dike Company employs Chester Wilcox as its chief foreman. Its isolated crossroads house becomes the planned site of a Scowrer attack intended to kill Wilcox and everyone with him.

records.l: the Crow Hill murders, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Crow Hill murders occur at the Crow Hill mine: Andrews and another assassin shoot manager Josiah H. Dunn, kill engineer Menzies after he attacks them, and escape unidentified through the mist.

records.l: the planned attack on Chester Wilcox, The Valley of Fear
records.s: A planned house bombing targets Chester Wilcox at the isolated Iron Dike crossroads. Boss McGinty assigns Jack McMurdo, Manders, and Reilly to kill him with blasting powder, despite the danger to Wilcox’s wife, three children, and hired help. The men detonate quarry powder at the house, but the attack is foiled because Wilcox had already relocated.

records.l: isolated house (Chester Wilcox's house), The Valley of Fear
records.s: An isolated house in an adjacent valley, about five miles from town, where Chester Wilcox had lived; after Wilcox moved his family away, McMurdo and companions destroyed the empty house with quarry powder.

records.l: destruction of Chester Wilcox's house, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_caused_by gunpowder McMurdo, Manders, and Reilly blew up Chester Wilcox's house with quarry powder. The explosion tore down the building, but it accomplished nothing because the house was empty.

records.l: shooting of Chester Wilcox, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_carried_out_from ambuscade Several weeks after the failed attack on his house, newspapers reported that Chester Wilcox had been shot at from an ambuscade. The text presents the shooting as connected to McMurdo's unfinished pursuit of him.

records.l: crimes of the Society of Freemen, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The topic recounts the Society of Freemen's crimes: planned shootings of Policemen Hunt and Evans, Mrs. Larbey's shooting, killings of the elder Jenkins and his brother, James Murdoch's mutilation, the Staphouse family's blowing up, and the Stendals' murders.

records.l: Steve Wilson, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Steve Wilson is Birdy Edwards’s undercover alias, lodging at Hobson’s Patch, posing as a reporter, gathering Scowrers information from McMurdo, and sending coded telegraphs.

records.l: Pinkerton’s, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Pinkerton’s is a detective organization employed by corporations and railroads to investigate and prosecute the Scowrers. It assigns its best investigator, Birdy Edwards, to secretly infiltrate and dismantle the group, with only Captain Marvin and employers knowing his identity.

records.l: the corporations, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Five corporations and two railroads unite, employing Pinkerton to investigate, gather evidence, and destroy the Scowrers.

records.l: the lodge meeting, The Valley of Fear
records.s: occurs_on Saturday evening [the regular lodge night] At the lodge meeting, McMurdo claims urgency and announces that Birdy Edwards is investigating the Scowrers. The members choose a committee, and the leaders agree to lure Edwards to McMurdo’s house and kill him.

records.l: the investigation of the Scowrers, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_conducted_by Birdy Edwards [under Pinkerton’s orders] The investigation is being conducted by Pinkerton for five corporations and two railroads. Birdy Edwards is collecting evidence that could send members of the lodge to prison.

records.l: the Scowrers’ violence, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Scowrers’ violence has been so constant that their members have treated it as part of ordinary life. The possibility of legal retribution now makes them confront the consequences of the violence they have inflicted on others.

records.l: the planned killing of Birdy Edwards, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_planned_by the Scowrers [as a response to the investigation] McMurdo proposes telling Birdy Edwards that he can sell him the lodge’s secrets and arranging a meeting at Widow MacNamara’s house. The lodge leaders plan to gather there, shut the door behind Edwards, and kill him.

records.l: the threat to the lodge, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_a Pinkerton investigation [potentially capable of destroying the lodge] The threat to the lodge comes from Birdy Edwards’s investigation and from the financial and organizational support of the corporations and railroads. McMurdo warns that Edwards may already obtain the lodge’s secrets and that his evidence could send every man present to prison.

records.l: the letter from Morris’s friend, The Valley of Fear
records.s: reports the investigation of the Scowrers [warns that Pinkerton is involved] The letter reports that five corporations and two railroads have organized against the Scowrers and that Pinkerton’s best investigator, Birdy Edwards, is operating in the valley. Its postscript says the information was written in a cipher handled daily in the telegraph service.

records.l: the secret investigation, The Valley of Fear
records.s: uses the cipher [to conceal telegraphed reports] The secret investigation is being carried out by Birdy Edwards under the false identity of Steve Wilson. He poses as a reporter, asks questions about the Scowrers, and transmits coded messages through the telegraph bureau.

records.l: the escape plan, The Valley of Fear
records.s: McMurdo tells Ettie Shafter that he may need to flee the valley and instructs her to come to the depot waiting room whenever he sends word. He intends to take her to the place where he came from and leave her with a good woman until they can marry.

records.l: the capture of the Scowrers, The Valley of Fear
records.s: is_a planned police operation [engineered by Birdy Edwards] The capture of the Scowrers takes place at McMurdo’s isolated house. Edwards admits his identity, while Captain Marvin and forty armed men surround the building, force the gang to surrender, and take its members into custody.

records.l: trial of the Scowrers, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The trial is held far from the Valley of Fear to prevent intimidation. Edwards’ unshaken testimony exposes the Scowrers’ organization and crimes, leading to McGinty and eight followers being executed, others imprisoned, and the Scowrers scattered.

records.l: Palmyra, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The Palmyra carried John Douglas and his companions toward South Africa. It reached Cape Town after Douglas was reported lost overboard in a gale off St. Helena.

records.l: the enigmatic note, The Valley of Fear
records.s: has_no superscription or signature The enigmatic note was slipped into Sherlock Holmes's letter box two months after the trial. It read, "Dear me, Mr. Holmes. Dear me!" and had neither a superscription nor a signature; Holmes treated it as evidence of deviltry.

records.l: the cable reporting John Douglas's death, The Valley of Fear
records.s: reports John Douglas's disappearance at sea [in a gale off St. Helena] The cable reporting John Douglas's death was sent by Ivy Douglas to Cecil Barker. It stated that Jack had been lost overboard in a gale off St. Helena and that the circumstances were unknown, but Holmes believed the report concealed a staged murder.

records.l: John Douglas's disappearance at sea, The Valley of Fear
records.s: John Douglas's disappearance at sea was reported as a gale-related fall overboard off St. Helena, but Sherlock Holmes assessed it as murder.

records.l: the planned murder of John Douglas, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The planned murder of John Douglas was carried out through a London-based criminal operation associated with Moriarty. Holmes describes it as an unusually elaborate use of a great brain and a large organization to ensure Douglas's destruction.

records.l: the danger to John Douglas in England, The Valley of Fear
records.s: The danger to John Douglas in England was considered greater than the danger he had escaped. Holmes advised his wife to get him out of England at any cost because he believed there was no safety for him there.

records.l: Moriarty's criminal operation, The Valley of Fear
records.s: targets John Douglas [for extinction] Moriarty's criminal operation involved locating John Douglas, advising on how to deal with him, and finally taking direct action when an agent failed. Holmes recognized the operation as the work of a master criminal rather than the Scowrers' crude violence.

records.l: Holmes's planned counteraction, The Valley of Fear
records.s: Holmes's planned counteraction is foreshadowed as he seeks time to devise a response to defeat Professor Moriarty.
